sanskrit_sloka:
తాని సర్వాణి సంయమ్య యుక్త ఆసీత మత్పరః ।
వశే హి యస్యేంద్రియాణి తస్య ప్రజ్ఞా ప్రతిష్ఠితాః ।। 61 ।।
translation_en: Those who keep their senses under control and always fix their mind on Me, they are in perfect knowledge.
explanation_en: The instruction to keep the senses restrained while fixing the mind on Krishna specifically adds something the tortoise metaphor alone doesn't capture: withdrawal by itself isn't enough. The attention has to be redirected somewhere, not just pulled back into a vacuum, or it drifts right back to where it started.

sanskrit_sloka:
ధ్యాయతో విషయాన్ పుంసః సంగస్తేషూపజాయతే ।
సంగాత్ సంజాయతే కామః కామాత్ క్రోధోఽభిజాయతే ।। 62 ।।
translation_en: Dwelling on sense objects increases lust for them. This interest gives rise to desires, and from those desires arises anger.
explanation_en: Krishna begins tracing a chain reaction here — dwelling on sense objects breeds attachment, attachment breeds desire — that reads almost like a diagnosis of how ordinary frustration and craving actually build inside a person, one small mental habit compounding into the next.

sanskrit_sloka:
క్రోధాద్భవతి సమ్మోహః సమ్మోహాత్ స్మృతివిభ్రమః ।
స్మృతిభ్రంశాద్బుద్ధి నాశో బుద్ధినాశాత్ ప్రణశ్యతి ।। 63 ।।
translation_en: Anger leads to indiscretion, which causes illusory memory. When there is amnesia, the mind perishes. When the mind perishes, man falls.
explanation_en: The chain continues its collapse: anger clouds judgment, clouded judgment corrupts memory, corrupted memory destroys discernment, and a person who has lost discernment is described, starkly, as fallen. It's less a moral warning than a mechanical description — this is simply what happens, step by step, when the earlier links aren't interrupted.

sanskrit_sloka:
రాగద్వేషవియుక్తైస్తు విషయానింద్రియైశ్చరన్ ।
ఆత్మవశ్యైర్విధేయాత్మా ప్రసాదమధిగచ్ఛతి ।। 64 ।।
translation_en: One who controls the mind and is free from mamkara-dwesha even while using sense objects/objects is eligible for the grace of God.
explanation_en: The way out isn't total avoidance of sense objects, Krishna clarifies, but engaging with them free of the attraction and aversion that usually accompany contact. Someone who has mastered this — using the senses without being hijacked by them — becomes fit to receive grace, not through withdrawal but through a changed relationship to engagement itself.

sanskrit_sloka:
ప్రసాదే సర్వ దుఃఖానాం హానిరస్యోపజాయతే ।
ప్రసన్నచేతసో హ్యాశు బుద్ధిః పర్యవతిష్ఠతే ।। 65 ।।
translation_en: By Bhagwat's grace one gets the supreme peace in which all sorrows are removed. Thus the intellect of one with a happy mind is quick and fixed in God.
explanation_en: Grace brings a peace that removes sorrow at its root, and from that peace, Krishna says, the intellect becomes swift and firmly established. There's an implied order here: peace isn't the reward for a sharp intellect; a settled intellect is what becomes possible once peace has already arrived.

sanskrit_sloka:
నాస్తి బుద్ధిరయుక్తస్య న చాయుక్తస్య భావనా ।
న చాభావయతః శాంతిః అశాంతస్య కుతః సుఖమ్ ।। 66 ।।
translation_en: One who is undisciplined and does not control the mind and senses, there is no stable intellect, no steady meditation of Bhagavat. He who never unites his mind with God has no peace. How can one who lacks peace of mind be happy?
explanation_en: Krishna traces the opposite failure mode with equal precision: without discipline, there's no stable understanding; without stable understanding, no real meditation; without meditation, no peace. The closing question — how can someone without peace be happy — isn't rhetorical flourish, it's the logical conclusion of everything just laid out.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఇంద్రియాణాం హి చరతాం యన్మనోఽనువిధీయతే ।
తదస్య హరతి ప్రజ్ఞాం వాయుర్నావమివాంభసి ।। 67 ।।
translation_en: Just as a strong wind pushes a boat off its course in water, it drains the mind if the mind is concentrated on any one sense.
explanation_en: The image of a strong wind driving a boat off course gives real force to what might otherwise sound like a mild warning: letting the mind fixate on even a single sense object is enough to derail the whole undertaking, the way one gust can undo a carefully plotted route.

తస్మాద్యస్య మహాబాహో నిగృహీతాని సర్వశః ।
ఇంద్రియాణీంద్రియార్థేభ్యః తస్య ప్రజ్ఞా ప్రతిష్ఠితా ।। 68 ।।

explanation_en: Krishna returns to the necessity of full sensory restraint, and the repetition after the boat metaphor feels earned rather than redundant — having just shown how easily one unguarded point capsizes the whole effort, the instruction to withdraw the senses completely now carries more weight than it did earlier in the chapter.

translation_en: What is day for all demons is the night of ignorance for the scholar, and what is night for all demons is day for the introverted sage.
explanation_en: The paradox that what's night for ordinary beings is day for the disciplined sage, and vice versa, captures something true about how radically different a life oriented toward inner reality looks from the outside. తద్వత్ కామా యం ప్రవిశంతి సర్వే

విహాయ కామాన్యః  సర్వాన్పుమాంశ్చరతి  నిఃస్పృహః ।

sanskrit_sloka:
ఏషా బ్రాహ్మీ స్థితిః పార్థ నైనాం ప్రాప్య విముహ్యతి ।
స్థిత్వాస్యామంతకాలేఽపి బ్రహ్మనిర్వాణమృచ్ఛతి ।। 72 ।।
translation_en: O Partha, what is the state of an enlightened soul, once enlightened it never again falls into delusion.  Even at the time of death, such a person who is steadfast in this wisdom, is freed from the cycle of birth and death and reaches the divine abode of that Lord.
explanation_en: The chapter's closing promise — that this state, once attained, doesn't collapse even at the moment of death, and leads beyond the cycle of rebirth entirely — gives Krishna's whole teaching in this chapter its ultimate stakes. Everything argued here isn't a lifestyle preference; it's presented as the difference between remaining caught in the cycle and finally stepping free of it.

sanskrit_sloka:
['అర్జున ఉవాచ ।
జ్యాయసీ చేత్కర్మణస్తే మతా బుద్ధిర్జనార్దన ।
తత్కిం కర్మణి ఘోరే మాం నియోజయసి కేశవ ।। 1 ।।', 'వ్యామిశ్రేణేవ వాక్యేన బుద్ధిం మోహయసీవ మే ।
తదేకం వద నిశ్చిత్య యేన శ్రేయోఽహమాప్నుయామ్ ।। 2 ।।']
translation_en: Arjuna said: O Janardhana, if knowledge is better than karma, then why do you want me to fight this terrible battle? My mind was bewildered by your vague instruction. Kindly instruct me that one way which will bring me the best prosperity.
explanation_en: Arjuna's frustration here is understandable: Krishna has just praised the person who sits in equanimity, unmoved by sense objects, and Arjuna hears this as an endorsement of withdrawal. His question isn't really about philosophy — it's a plea for a simpler answer than the one he's getting. He wants to be told which single path to take, not asked to hold two truths at once. This impatience with complexity is itself part of what Krishna is about to correct.

sanskrit_sloka:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ ।
లోకేఽస్మిన్ ద్వివిధా నిష్ఠా పురా ప్రోక్తా మయానఘ  ।
జ్ఞానయోగేన సాంఖ్యానాం కర్మయోగేన యోగినామ్  ।। 3 ।।
translation_en: The Lord thus spoke: O sinless one, there are two paths to Bhagavat-prapti (enlightenment) which have been told by me earlier: the path of knowledge for those interested in meditative devotion; Karma Marga for those interested in work.
explanation_en: Krishna's distinction between the path of knowledge and the path of action isn't a menu of options — it's an acknowledgment that people are wired differently. Some find their way to truth through contemplation, others through engaged work in the world. By naming both as legitimate, Krishna quietly closes off Arjuna's hope that one path is superior and easier than the other.

sanskrit_sloka:
న కర్మణామనారంభాత్ నైష్కర్మ్యం పురుషోఽశ్నుతే ।
న చ సన్న్యసనాదేవ సిద్ధిం సమధిగచ్ఛతి ।। 4 ।।
translation_en: Man cannot be freed from karmic bondage (pratikriya) without performing karmas. Also, only through external (physical) asceticism one attains Jnana Siddhi.
explanation_en: The claim that inaction cannot free anyone from karmic bondage cuts against a common spiritual fantasy: that if you simply stop doing things, you stop accumulating consequences. Krishna is dismantling this before Arjuna can retreat into it. Physical withdrawal from action, without inner transformation, isn't liberation — it's just idleness wearing liberation's clothes.

sanskrit_sloka:
న హి కశ్చిత్ క్షణమపి జాతు తిష్ఠత్యకర్మకృత్ ।
కార్యతే హ్యవశః కర్మ సర్వః ప్రకృతిజైర్గుణైః ।। 5 ।।
translation_en: No one can stop practicing karma even for a single moment. In fact, all living beings are motivated by their inherent nature (tri-gunas) to perform karma.
explanation_en: Krishna's observation that no one can avoid action even for an instant is almost a provocation aimed at anyone tempted by renunciation as escape. Breathing, thinking, existing — all of it is action, driven by the same forces of nature that move everything else. The fantasy of a neutral, actionless life was never available to begin with.

sanskrit_sloka:
కర్మేంద్రియాణి సంయమ్య య ఆస్తే మనసా స్మరన్ ।
ఇంద్రియార్థాన్ విమూఢాత్మా మిథ్యాచారః స ఉచ్యతే ।। 6 ।।
translation_en: Those who keep their external senses under control, but think only about the things of the senses in their minds, are self-deluders, and such people are called hypocrites.
explanation_en: This verse targets a specific kind of self-deception: the person who looks disciplined on the outside — senses restrained, posture composed — while their mind is still chewing on the very things they claim to have renounced. Krishna doesn't soften this; he calls it what it is, a form of hypocrisy. Outer restraint without inner honesty fools everyone except the person doing it.

sanskrit_sloka:
యస్త్వింద్రియాణి మనసా నియమ్యారభతేఽర్జున ।
కర్మేంద్రియైః కర్మయోగమసక్తః స విశిష్యతే ।। 7 ।।
translation_en: But, Arjuna, the Karma Yogis who control their sense organs with the mind and work without mamkara/interests with the Karmandriyas, are truly excellent.
explanation_en: The contrast Krishna draws is subtle but important: it's not about doing more or doing less, but about where the control originates. Someone who acts with the mind actively governing the senses, without personal stake in the outcome, is operating from a completely different place than someone merely restraining themselves by willpower. One is integration; the other is suppression.

sanskrit_sloka:
నియతం కురు కర్మ త్వం కర్మ జ్యాయో హ్యకర్మణః ।
శరీరయాత్రాపి చ తే న ప్రసిద్ధ్యేదకర్మణః ।। 8 ।।
translation_en: So you should perform the prescribed duty in accordance with the Vedas, because doing things is better than inaction (abiding).  Even maintenance of the body is not possible due to leaving out activities.
explanation_en: Krishna's instruction to perform one's prescribed duty sounds almost mundane after the metaphysics of the previous chapter, and that's the point — spiritual understanding has to land somewhere practical. Even the body itself can't be sustained without some activity. There is no version of human life, however elevated the philosophy, that doesn't require doing something.

sanskrit_sloka:
యజ్ఞార్ధాత్ కర్మణోఽన్యత్ర  లోకోఽయం  కర్మబంధనః  ।
తదర్థం కర్మ కౌంతేయ ముక్తసంగః సమాచర ।। 9 ।।
translation_en: Works should be done like a yajna, an offering to Bhagavat, or else those works will tie us in karmic bonds in this world.  Therefore, O son of Kunti, perform the duties assigned to you, without interest in their results, for the satisfaction of God.
explanation_en: By framing work as an offering rather than a personal project, Krishna reframes the entire question of motivation. Work done for oneself creates attachment and binds; work done as sacrifice releases. The difference isn't in the task but in who the doer believes it's for. This single shift in orientation is what separates labor from bondage.

sanskrit_sloka:
సహయజ్ఞాః ప్రజాః సృష్ట్వా పురోవాచ ప్రజాపతిః ।
అనేన ప్రసవిష్యధ్వమేష వోఽస్త్విష్టకామధుక్ ।। 10 ।।
translation_en: At the beginning of creation, Lord Brahma, who created mankind along with their duties, said, "Prosper by performing these yajnas. These fulfill all your desires."
explanation_en: Krishna reaches back to the very beginning of creation to root this teaching in something older than personal preference. The idea that duties were given alongside creation itself — not invented later as rules — gives the instruction a kind of built-in legitimacy. Prosperity, in this framing, was never meant to come from hoarding, but from participating in an exchange.

sanskrit_sloka:
దేవాన్ భావయతానేన తే దేవా భావయంతు వః ।
పరస్పరం భావయంతః శ్రేయః పరమవాప్స్యథ ।। 11 ।।
translation_en: Gods will be pleased by your yajnas. The mutual cooperation of Gods and humans brings prosperity to all.
explanation_en: The picture of gods and humans sustaining one another complicates any purely individualistic reading of spiritual life. Nobody flourishes in isolation, not even at the cosmic level. This verse quietly argues that the highest good is always relational — a mutual nourishing, not a solitary achievement.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఇష్టాన్ భోగాన్ హి వో దేవా దాస్యంతే యజ్ఞభావితాః  ।
తైర్ధత్తానప్రదాయైభ్యో యో భుంక్తే స్తేన ఏవ సః  ।। 12 ।।
translation_en: The deities, who are satisfied with the performance of yajnas, bestow all that is necessary for the maintenance of life. Those who enjoy what is given to them, without reporting it back to the gods, are thieves indeed.
explanation_en: Krishna's warning about taking without offering back has an edge to it — he's not being gentle about entitlement. Enjoying the benefits that come from a larger system while contributing nothing to it is, in his terms, simple theft. This applies as easily to ecological and social systems today as it did to ritual sacrifice then.

sanskrit_sloka:
యజ్ఞశిష్టాశినః  సంతో  ముచ్యంతే సర్వకిల్బిషైః ।
భుంజతే తే త్వఘం పాపా యే పచంత్యాత్మకారణాత్  ।। 13 ।।
translation_en: The spiritual minded good men who eat only the rest of the food reported first in the Yajna will be freed from all sins. Those who cook rice for their own pleasure eat sin.
explanation_en: There's a striking generosity embedded in this verse: the good are freed of sin precisely because they eat only what remains after offering, not because they're inherently superior people. It's the posture of gratitude and giving-first that purifies, not personal virtue in the abstract. Selfish consumption, by contrast, is described almost literally as consuming sin.

sanskrit_sloka:
అన్నాద్భవంతి భూతాని పర్జన్యాదన్నసంభవః ।
యజ్ఞాద్భవతి పర్జన్యో యజ్ఞః కర్మసముద్భవః  ।। 14 ।।

explanation_en: This verse traces a chain — rain to food to life — that could easily read as agricultural trivia if not for what it implies: human sustenance is embedded in a much larger cycle that our individual choices either support or disrupt. Krishna is quietly arguing that dutiful action isn't separate from the natural world; it's part of what keeps that world functioning.

sanskrit_sloka:
కర్మ బ్రహ్మోద్భవం విద్ధి బ్రహ్మాక్షరసముధ్భవమ్ ।

explanation_en: By tracing prescribed duty back through the Vedas to the Lord himself, Krishna is answering an unspoken question Arjuna hasn't voiced yet: why should I trust that any of this matters? The chain of origin he lays out is his answer — duty isn't arbitrary convention, it has a source, and that source is ultimately divine.

translation_en: Those who do not fulfill their obligation in this yajna cycle prescribed by the Vedas are sinners. They live only for their sensual pleasures; So their life is wasted.
explanation_en: The condemnation here is sharp: those who ignore this cycle of mutual duty and live only for their senses are called sinners whose lives are wasted. It's a hard line, but it clarifies what Krishna considers the actual failure mode of a human life — not ambition or effort, but self-enclosed pleasure-seeking disconnected from any larger purpose.

translation_en: But those who are happy in the soul, with perfect knowledge and contented in the soul, have no duty.
explanation_en: This verse offers the exception that proves the rule: the person who has found complete satisfaction in the Self genuinely has no duty left to perform, because duty exists to move a person toward that satisfaction in the first place. Once you've arrived, the instructions that got you there no longer apply — not because they were wrong, but because their job is done.

sanskrit_sloka:
నైవ తస్య  కృతేనార్థో నాకృతేనేహ కశ్చన  ।

translation_en: Such enlightened souls have nothing to gain or lose (gains and losses) from doing or not doing their duties (karmas).  There is no need for them to depend on other beings for their selfish benefit.
explanation_en: Krishna describes someone so thoroughly settled that gain and loss have stopped mattering to them, whether from acting or not acting. This isn't apathy — it's the far side of engagement, reached after passing through it rather than by avoiding it. explanation_en: The stakes Krishna names here are enormous — the collapse of worlds, chaos for all beings — if he were to stop acting. sanskrit_sloka:

explanation_en: Describing those whose actions have burned away every trace of craving for material reward as 'pandits' — the genuinely learned — redefines wisdom away from book knowledge and toward a specific inner accomplishment: the exhaustion of self-interested motive through disciplined action itself.

sanskrit_sloka:

sanskrit_sloka:

explanation_en: The claim that a person acting only with the body, mind fully governed, free of possessiveness, incurs no sin even while still doing karma pushes the argument to its logical edge. sanskrit_sloka:

explanation_en: Contentment with whatever comes, freedom from envy, and equanimity through the ups and downs of pleasure and pain, success and failure — this cluster of qualities describes someone whose inner stability doesn't depend on outcomes going their way. sanskrit_sloka:

explanation_en: By listing worship through material offering alongside worship through offering the self directly into 'the fire of supreme truth,' Krishna places ritual practice and radical self-surrender on the same continuum. translation_en: Those who know the secret of Yajna, perform it, receive its immortal essence, and progress towards the Supreme Truth. O noble one of the Kuru clan, those who do not perform any kind of yajna, will not get any happiness either in this world or in the next.
explanation_en: The claim that those who understand sacrifice attain its 'immortal essence' and move toward the Supreme, while those who perform no sacrifice at all find no happiness in this world or the next, is stark. translation_en: Those who lack knowledge and faith and have a doubting nature will fall away. Those who have no faith and doubt will have no happiness in this world or in the Hereafter.
explanation_en: The warning about those without knowledge, without faith, and given to doubt is severe: no happiness in this world or the next. translation_en: Offering the fruits of all activities to the Lord, Karma Yogis attain eternal peace. At the same time, those who are motivated by their kama (desires) and act for selfish gain, become entangled in karmic bonds because they are interested in karmic fruits.
explanation_en: The contrast between those who offer their results away and find peace, versus those chasing personal desire and ending up entangled, is almost mechanical in its logic: the same action, aimed at different targets, produces opposite outcomes. translation_en: Soul-tempered and dispassionate living souls, knowing that they are neither the doer nor the cause of anything, are happy in this city of nine gates.
explanation_en: Calling the body a 'city of nine gates' — the openings of perception and expulsion — gives a vivid, almost architectural image for embodied life. translation_en: But, for those whose ignorance of the soul is destroyed by the divine spiritual knowledge, that knowledge illumines the Supreme Soul, as the sun illumines all in the day.
explanation_en: The sun metaphor for knowledge dispelling ignorance is common enough to feel almost automatic, but its precision matters here: sunlight doesn't argue ignorance out of existence, it simply illuminates, and darkness has no independent power to resist it. explanation_en: The distinction between striving as the tool for a beginner and stillness as the tool for someone advanced acknowledges that spiritual practice isn't static — what actually helps a person changes as they progress. Effort gets you moving; only later does effort itself need to give way to something quieter.

explanation_en: Disinterest in both sense objects and personal karmic reward is named as the marker of real advancement here — not disinterest in life itself, but in the specific mechanism of craving results. It's a narrow, precise target, not a blanket call to indifference.

translation_en: Yogis who have conquered the mind - cold, happy, sad, and angry - are above these dualities. Such Yogis are calm and have a fixed will in devotion to God.
explanation_en: Someone who has mastered the mind stays level through cold and heat, joy and sorrow, praise and blame — not because these stop happening, but because the person's stability no longer depends on which one shows up. Krishna is describing a fixed center that outward weather can't move.

translation_en: Benefactors, friends, enemies, saints and sinners – yogis look with impartiality. translation_en: Those who want to attain the state of yoga should be in meditation of Bhagavat with controlled mind-body, renouncing desires and pleasures, and in seclusion.

sanskrit_sloka:
యం లబ్ద్వా చాపరం లాభం మన్యతే నాధికం తతః  ।
యస్మిన్  స్థితో న దుఃఖేన గురుణాపి విచాల్యతే  ।। 22 ।।
translation_en: After attaining that status, Marinka feels that nothing is better than that. He who is thus established, is unmoved even in severe sorrows.
explanation_en: Having reached this state, Krishna says, a person feels nothing else compares — and crucially, remains unmoved even by severe sorrow. This isn't emotional numbness; it's a description of something so foundational that ordinary suffering, while still felt, no longer has the power to uproot it.

sanskrit_sloka:
తం విద్యాద్ దుఃఖసంయోగవియోగం యోగసంజ్ఞితమ్ ।
స నిశ్చయేన యోక్తవ్యో యోగోఽనిర్విణ్ణచేతసా ।। 23 ।।
translation_en: Yoga is the state of being freed from sorrows.  This yoga should be practiced with firm resolve without any pessimism/disbelief;
explanation_en: Defining yoga plainly as freedom from sorrow, and insisting it be pursued with firm resolve rather than doubt or discouragement, Krishna cuts through any temptation to treat the practice as merely aspirational. He wants conviction behind the effort, not tentative half-belief.

sanskrit_sloka: ['సంకల్పప్రభవాన్ కామాన్ త్యక్త్వా సర్వానశేషతః ।\nమనసైవేంద్రియగ్రామం వినియమ్య సమంతతః ।। 24 ।।', 'శనైః శనైరుపరమేత్ బుద్ధ్యా ధృతిగృహీతయా ।\nఆత్మసంస్థం మనః  కృత్వా న కించిదపి చింతయేత్ ।। 25 ।।']
translation_en: One should give up all desires arising from worldly thoughts and restrain the senses from all sides with the mind. Gradually and surely, with firm faith in Buddhi, the mind becomes fixed in God and thinks of nothing else.
explanation_en: Krishna's instruction to give up desires 'arising from worldly thoughts' pinpoints something specific: not all desire, but the kind manufactured by the mind's habitual planning and imagining. That's a narrower, more actionable target than trying to eliminate wanting altogether.

sanskrit_sloka: ['సంకల్పప్రభవాన్ కామాన్ త్యక్త్వా సర్వానశేషతః ।\nమనసైవేంద్రియగ్రామం వినియమ్య సమంతతః ।। 24 ।।', 'శనైః శనైరుపరమేత్ బుద్ధ్యా ధృతిగృహీతయా ।\nఆత్మసంస్థం మనః  కృత్వా న కించిదపి చింతయేత్ ।। 25 ।।']
translation_en: One should give up all desires arising from worldly thoughts and restrain the senses from all sides with the mind. Gradually and surely, with firm faith in Buddhi, the mind becomes fixed in God and thinks of nothing else.
explanation_en: The instruction to gradually and steadily withdraw the mind into stillness, using firm conviction rather than force, describes patience as a method in itself — this isn't a sudden achievement but a slow, deliberate settling, repeated until it becomes natural.

sanskrit_sloka:
యతో యతో నిశ్చరతి మనశ్చంచలమస్థిరం ।
తతస్తతో నియమ్యైతదాత్మన్యేవ వశం నయేత్ ।। 26 ।।
translation_en: Whenever and wherever this fickle, unstable mind wanders, it should be brought back and constantly focused on God.
explanation_en: Krishna's instruction to simply bring the wandering mind back, again and again, wherever it strays, is almost startlingly unsentimental about the process. There's no drama here, no failure implied by the wandering itself — just the plain, repeated act of returning.

sanskrit_sloka:
ప్రశాంతమనసం హ్యేనం యోగినం సుఖముత్తమమ్ ।
ఉపైతి శాంతరజసం బ్రహ్మభూతమకల్మషమ్ ।। 27 ।।
translation_en: A Yogi who is calm in mind, calm in his passions, sinless, who sees everything in relation to Bhagavat – attains the highest transcendental bliss.
explanation_en: The state of highest bliss is tied here to seeing everything specifically in relation to the divine — not seeing less of the world, but seeing all of it through a single unifying lens. Calm mind, calm passions, and freedom from sin are named as its accompanying conditions, not separate achievements.

sanskrit_sloka:
యుంజన్నేవం సదాత్మానం యోగీ విగతకల్మషః  ।
సుఖేన బ్రహ్మసంస్పర్శ మత్యంతం  సుఖమశ్నుతే  ।। 28 ।।
translation_en: A self-restrained yogi unites the soul with God, attains freedom from material impurities, and attains the highest state of absolute bliss, always in union with the Supreme.
explanation_en: Union with the divine, freedom from impurity, and constant contact with the highest bliss are described as the natural outcome of sustained self-restraint — Krishna presents these not as separate rewards but as facets of a single unfolding state reached through the same discipline.

sanskrit_sloka:
సర్వభూతస్థమాత్మానం  సర్వభూతాని చాత్మని  ।
ఈక్షతే యోగయుక్తాత్మా సర్వత్ర  సమదర్శనః  ।। 29 ।।
translation_en: True yogis unite the inner mind with God and see all demons in God and God in all demons.
explanation_en: Seeing all beings within the divine and the divine within all beings marks a significant expansion from the earlier equanimity toward objects and people — here the unifying vision becomes genuinely cosmic, collapsing the boundary between self, others, and the sacred entirely.
word_by_word_meaning_en: sarva-bhuta-stham — abiding in all beings; atmanam — the supreme soul; sarva — all; bhutani — living beings; Cha — and; atmani — in the Lord; eksate — seeing; yoga-yukta-atma — united with the Lord in antahkarana; sarvatra — everywhere; sama-darshanah — equanimity of vision.

sanskrit_sloka:
యో మాం పశ్యతి సర్వత్ర సర్వం చ మయి పశ్యతి ।
తస్యాహం న ప్రణశ్యామి స చ మే న ప్రణశ్యతి ।। 30 ।।
translation_en: He who beholds Me in all, who beholds all in Me, will not miss Me, and I will not miss them.
explanation_en: The reciprocal promise — whoever sees Krishna everywhere will never lose him, and Krishna will never lose that person — reframes the whole pursuit as fundamentally relational rather than achievement-based. It isn't a technique that earns a prize; it's a perception that, once genuinely held, secures a bond that doesn't break.

sanskrit_sloka:
సర్వభూతస్థితం యో మాం  భజత్యేకత్వమాస్థితః  ।
సర్వథా వర్తమానోఽపి స యోగీ  మయి వర్తతే  ।। 31 ।।
translation_en: The Yogi who is one with Me and worships Me as the Supreme Being who is present in all the demons, doing all kinds of activities, lives in Me.
explanation_en: Worshipping the Supreme Being as present within all beings while still engaged in every kind of ordinary activity closes the gap between contemplative withdrawal and active life that the chapter opened with — devotion, at this level, doesn't require stepping outside the world at all.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఆత్మౌపమ్యేన సర్వత్ర సమం పశ్యతి యోఽర్జున ।
సుఖం వా యది వా దుఃఖం స యోగీ పరమో మతః ।। 32 ।।
translation_en: I consider those who treat all beings equally and respond to the happiness and sorrows of others as if they were their own, as perfect yogis.
explanation_en: Krishna's definition of the perfect yogi as someone who feels others' joy and sorrow as their own moves the whole discussion from private attainment into empathy. Equanimity, by this point in the chapter, has quietly become something closer to compassion.

sanskrit_sloka:
అర్జున ఉవాచ ।
యోఽయం యోగస్త్వయా  ప్రోక్తః సామ్యేన మధుసూదన ।
ఏతస్యాహం న పశ్యామి  చంచలత్వాత్ స్థితిం స్థిరామ్  ।। 33 ।।
translation_en: Arjuna said: O Madhusudana, this method of yoga that you mentioned, because of this restless mind, seems to me impracticable and impossible.
explanation_en: Arjuna's objection — that this method sounds impossible given how restless the mind actually is — is refreshingly honest. He isn't rejecting the philosophy; he's pointing out a real practical obstacle that anyone who has tried to meditate will recognize immediately.

sanskrit_sloka:
చంచలం హి మనః కృష్ణ ప్రమాథి బలవద్ధృడమ్ ।
తస్యాహం నిగ్రహం మన్యే వాయోరివ సుదుష్కరమ్  ।। 34 ।।
translation_en: This mind is very restless, turbulent, strong and stubborn. Controlling it seems more difficult than controlling the wind, O Krishna.
explanation_en: Comparing the mind's difficulty to controlling the wind gives real weight to Arjuna's doubt — it's not a minor complaint, it's a comparison to something famously, almost proverbially uncontrollable. He isn't being lazy; he's naming a genuinely hard problem.

sanskrit_sloka:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ ।
అసంశయం మహాబాహో మనో దుర్నిగ్రహం చలమ్  ।
అభ్యాసేన తు కౌంతేయ వైరాగ్యేణ  చ గృహ్యతే ।। 35 ।।
translation_en: Sri Krishna Paramatma said: O son of Kunti with great arms, you are right; The mind is indeed very difficult to control. But, it can be tamed by practice and dispassion.
explanation_en: Krishna doesn't dismiss the difficulty — he confirms it outright, agreeing the mind is indeed hard to control, before offering the two tools that actually work: practice and dispassion. The validation matters; it makes the subsequent advice land as realistic rather than dismissive.

sanskrit_sloka:
అసంయతాత్మనా యోగో  దుష్ప్రాప  ఇతి మే మతిః ।
వశ్యాత్మనా తు యతతా శక్యోఽవాప్తుముపాయతః  ।। 36 ।।
translation_en: Yoga is difficult for those who are not in control of the mind. But, those who learn to control the mind, and practice in the right way, can attain perfection in yoga. This is my opinion.
explanation_en: By stating plainly that yoga is difficult without self-control but achievable through right practice, Krishna keeps both truths in view at once — the difficulty is real, and so is the possibility. Neither cancels the other out.

sanskrit_sloka:
అర్జున ఉవాచ ।
అయతిః  శ్రద్ధయోపేతో యోగాచ్చలితమానసః ।
అప్రాప్య యోగసంసిద్ధిం కాం గతి కృష్ణ గచ్ఛతి ।। 37 ।।
translation_en: Arjuna said: What is the fate of the yogi who, even after starting this journey with diligence, due to a restless mind, does not exert enough effort and is unable to achieve the ultimate success of the goal of yoga in this life?
explanation_en: Arjuna's follow-up question — what happens to someone who starts sincerely but fails to finish — reveals genuine anxiety about wasted effort, a fear anyone who has abandoned a discipline partway through will recognize. It's less about doubting the path and more about fearing failure within it.

sanskrit_sloka:
కచ్చిన్నోభయవిభ్రష్టః ఛిన్నాభ్రమివ  నశ్యతి ।
అప్రతిష్ఠో  మహాబాహో విమూఢో  బ్రహ్మణః  పథి ।। 38 ।।
translation_en: O great-armed Krishna, is not one who strays from the path of yoga depraved of both material and spiritual attainments? Is he like a cloud that is parted and scattered and becomes confused?
explanation_en: The image of a scattered cloud, dissolved and confused, gives vivid shape to Arjuna's fear: that falling short of the goal might leave a person worse off than if they'd never tried — belonging fully to neither the worldly life they left nor the spiritual attainment they didn't reach.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఏతన్మే సంశయం కృష్ణ ఛేత్తుమర్హస్యశేషతః ।
త్వదన్యః సంశయస్యాస్య ఛేత్తా న హ్యుపపద్యతే ।। 39 ।।
translation_en: O Krishna, clear this doubt of mine completely, and who can do it better than you?
explanation_en: Arjuna's direct appeal — clear this doubt, who better than you to do it — shows real trust alongside real anxiety. He isn't demanding reassurance he doesn't believe in; he's asking the one source he actually considers capable of answering honestly.

sanskrit_sloka:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ ।
పార్థ నైవేహ నాముత్ర వినాశస్తత్య విద్యతే ।
న హి కల్యాణకృత్కశ్చిత్ దుర్గతిం తాత గచ్ఛతి ।। 40 ।।
translation_en: O Partha, he who is on the spiritual path will not perish either in this world or in the next world. Dear friend, one who strives for the attainment of Bhagwat will never suffer from Durga.
explanation_en: Krishna's reassurance is unambiguous: no one on this path is destroyed, in this world or beyond. It directly answers Arjuna's fear of falling into some kind of spiritual no-man's-land — sincere effort, Krishna insists, is never simply wasted.

sanskrit_sloka: ['ప్రాప్య పుణ్యకృతాం లోకానుషిత్వా శాశ్వతీః సమాః ।\nశుచీనాం  శ్రీమతాం గేహే యోగభ్రష్టోఽభిజాయతే  ।। 41 ।।', 'అథవా యోగినామేవ కులే భవతి ధీమతామ్ ।\nఏతద్ది దుర్లభతరం లోకే జన్మ యదీదృశమ్  ।। 42 ।।']
translation_en: Those who are depraved of yoga (those who could not achieve success in yoga in this life), go to the holy worlds. Pidapa, who lived there for a long time, will be born back in the earth, in a family of pious and wealthy people. Or, those who have developed Vairagya due to long practice of yoga, will be born in a family of divine knowledge.  Such a birth is very rare.
explanation_en: The description of someone who fell short of full success still being reborn into favorable circumstances — either wealth and virtue, or a family already oriented toward spiritual knowledge — reframes apparent failure as, at worst, a delay rather than a loss.

న మాం దుష్కృతినో మూఢాః ప్రపద్యంతే నరాధమాః ।
మాయయాపహృతజ్ఞానా ఆసురం భావమాశ్రితాః ।। 15 ।।
translation_en: Four kinds of men do not surrender to Me - those who lack knowledge, those who have the ability to know Me but lazily follow their lower nature, those who are deluded, and those who are endowed with asura power.
explanation_en: The four types who fail to surrender — the ignorant, the lazily self-indulgent who could know better, the deluded, and those given over to a demonic disposition — cover a wide spectrum of failure, from simple lack of exposure to active resistance, suggesting more than one root cause behind the same outcome.

sanskrit_sloka:
చతుర్విధా భజంతే మాం జనాః సుకృతినోఽర్జున ।
ఆర్తో జిజ్ఞాసురర్థార్థీ జ్ఞానీ చ భరతర్షభ ।। 16 ।।
translation_en: O best of Bharatas, four types of Dharma-parayanas engage in devotion to Me – those in distress, those who strive for the acquisition of knowledge, those who seek the acquisition of worldly goods, and those who are fixed on knowledge.
explanation_en: By contrast, the four types who do turn toward devotion — those in distress, seekers of knowledge, seekers of worldly gain, and the already wise — shows Krishna doesn't require pure motive as the price of entry. Even self-interested reasons for turning toward him are accepted as valid starting points.

sanskrit_sloka:
తేషాం జ్ఞానీ నిత్యయుక్త ఏకభక్తిర్విశిష్యతే ।
ప్రియో హి జ్ఞానినోఽత్యర్థమహం స చ మమ ప్రియః ।। 17 ।।
translation_en: Of all these, those who worship Me with wisdom, and those who have firm resolve and exclusive devotion to Me, I regard as the best of all.  I am dear to them and they are dear to me.
explanation_en: Among these four, Krishna singles out the wise devotee with single-minded focus as dearest to him, and reciprocates that closeness explicitly. It's a striking claim of mutual affection, not just approval — the relationship runs both directions.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఉదారాః సర్వ ఏవైతే జ్ఞానీ త్వాత్మైవ మే మతమ్ ।
ఆస్థితః స హి యుక్తాత్మా మామేవానుత్తమాం గతిమ్ ।। 18 ।।
translation_en: All those who are devoted to Me are truly the best. But those who are wise, firm in determination, whose intellect is united in Me, and who have Me alone as their ultimate goal, I consider to be My very form.
explanation_en: Calling the wise devotee 'my very form' pushes past ordinary praise into near-identification — suggesting that a certain quality of devotion doesn't just please Krishna from a distance but somehow merges with what he considers his own nature.

sanskrit_sloka:
బహూనాం జన్మనామంతే జ్ఞానవాన్ మాం ప్రపద్యతే ।
వాసుదేవః సర్వమితి స మహాత్మా సుదుర్లభః ।। 19 ।।
translation_en: After many births of spiritual practice, the wise one realizes that all that exists is Me (Vasudeva) and surrenders to Me. Such a Mahatma is very rare indeed.
explanation_en: The phrase 'after many births' matters here — this isn't presented as an instant epiphany but the fruit of accumulated practice across a long arc, arriving finally at the recognition that everything that exists is Krishna. Its rarity is named plainly: such a person is genuinely uncommon.

sanskrit_sloka:
కామైస్తైస్తైర్హృతజ్ఞానాః ప్రపద్యంతేఽన్యదేవతాః ।
తం తం నియమమాస్థాయ ప్రకృత్యా నియతాః స్వయా ।। 20 ।।
translation_en: Those who are lost in knowledge with material worldly desires surrender to other gods. They follow their own nature and worship other gods; Karma Kandas are performed to please the respective deities.
explanation_en: Krishna's description of those pursuing other deities as motivated by specific worldly desires, following their own inclination, isn't dismissive so much as diagnostic — he's identifying the logic behind different forms of worship rather than simply ranking them by moral worth.

sanskrit_sloka:
యో యో యాం యాం తనుం భక్తః శ్రద్ధయార్చితుమిచ్ఛతి ।
తస్య తస్యాచలాం శ్రద్ధాం తామేవ విదధామ్యహమ్ ।। 21 ।।
translation_en: Whichever form of deity a devotee wants to worship with faith, I will make that devotee focus on that form.
explanation_en: The promise that Krishna strengthens whatever form of devotion a person sincerely brings, whichever deity they choose, is remarkably generous — it locates the actual power behind any sincere worship in him, regardless of which name or form the devotee consciously directs it toward.

sanskrit_sloka:
స తయా శ్రద్ధయా యుక్తః తస్యారాధనమీహతే ।
లభతే చ తతః కామాన్మయైవ విహితాన్హి తాన్ ।। 22 ।।
translation_en: A devotee who has sraddha faith worships that deity and gets the desired material. But, in fact, I am the one who provides those benefits.
explanation_en: Faith directed at another deity still yields desired results, Krishna says, but he's careful to clarify the mechanism: it's ultimately him providing the benefit, even when the devotee doesn't recognize the source. Credit, so to speak, runs deeper than the immediate object of worship.

sanskrit_sloka:
అంతవత్తు ఫలం తేషాం తద్భవత్యల్పమేధసామ్ ।
దేవాన్ దేవయజో యాంతి మద్భక్తా యాంతి మామపి ।। 23 ।।
translation_en: But the fruit of these low-knowledge people is temporary. The worshipers of the deities go to the worlds of the respective deities, while My devotees reach Me.
explanation_en: The distinction between temporary fruit for those seeking lesser goals and reaching Krishna directly for those devoted to him isn't a punishment for the former — it's simply a description of where each kind of aim actually leads, proportional to what was sought.

sanskrit_sloka:
అవ్యక్తం వ్యక్తిమాపన్నం  మన్యంతే  మామబుద్ధయః  ।
పరం భావమజానంతో మమావ్యయమనుత్తమమ్  ।। 24 ।।
translation_en: The ignorant think that I, the Supreme Lord, Sri Krishna - who was once a formless immanence and has now assumed a form. They are unable to understand the literal, supreme form of this Self.
explanation_en: The ignorant assumption that Krishna's manifest form arose from formlessness misunderstands the relationship entirely — Krishna suggests his supreme nature was never actually formless to begin with in the way people imagine, and the confusion here is conceptual, not just factual.

sanskrit_sloka:
నాహం ప్రకాశః సర్వస్య యోగమాయాసమావృతః ।
మూఢోఽయం నాభిజానాతి లోకో మామజమవ్యయమ్ ।। 25 ।।
translation_en: Covered by my Yogamaya Shakti, I do not manifest to all. So the ignorant cannot know that I am birthless and changeless.
explanation_en: Describing himself as veiled by his own yogamaya, unseen by most, gives a theological reason for why divinity isn't self-evident to everyone: not absence, but a kind of active concealment that only lifts under specific conditions Krishna will describe as the chapters continue.

sanskrit_sloka:
వేదాహం సమతీతాని వర్తమానాని చార్జున ।
భవిష్యాణి చ భూతాని మాం తు వేద న కశ్చన ।। 26 ।।
translation_en: Arjuna! I know all things past, present, and future, and all living things; But I don't know anyone.
explanation_en: Krishna's claim to know all beings across past, present, and future, while adding pointedly that no one truly knows him, creates a striking asymmetry — complete knowledge flows one direction, and full reciprocal understanding isn't available to the ordinary seeker in the same measure.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఇచ్ఛాద్వేషసముత్థేన ద్వందమోహేన భారత ।
సర్వభూతాని సమ్మోహం సర్గే యాంతి పరంతప ।। 27 ।।
translation_en: O descendant of Bharata - Raga and hatred are dualities, arising from lust (delusion). O conqueror of enemies, every living being in this material world is deluded by these from birth itself.
explanation_en: Attributing the universal experience of attraction and aversion to a kind of delusion present 'from birth itself' normalizes this struggle rather than treating it as personal failure — every being enters the world already caught in this duality, according to Krishna, not through individual fault.

sanskrit_sloka:
యేషాం త్వంతగతం పాపం జనానాం పుణ్యకర్మణామ్ ।
తే ద్వంద్వమోహనిర్ముక్తా భజంతే మాం దృఢవ్రతాః  ।। 28 ।।
translation_en: Those whose sins are completely destroyed by performing pious activities are freed from the lust of these dualities. Such people worship Me with strong determination.
explanation_en: Freedom from this duality is tied here to accumulated virtuous action gradually dissolving sin — not a sudden switch but a threshold crossed through sustained right conduct, after which firm, undistracted worship of Krishna becomes possible.

sanskrit_sloka:
జరామరణమోక్షాయ మామాశ్రిత్య యతంతి యే ।
తే బ్రహ్మ తద్విదుః కృత్స్నమధ్యాత్మం కర్మ చాఖిలమ్ ।। 29 ।।
translation_en: Those who take refuge in Me, striving to be freed from old age and death, realize Brahman, their own soul, and the field of all karma.
explanation_en: Those seeking refuge specifically to be freed from old age and death are said to come to understand Brahman, the individual soul, and the entirety of action — Krishna links the very human fear of decline and mortality directly to the doorway into deeper metaphysical understanding.

sanskrit_sloka:
సాధిభూతాధిదైవం మాం సాధియజ్ఞం చ యే విదుః ।
ప్రయాణకాలేఽపి చ మాం తే విదుర్యుక్తచేతసః ।। 30 ।।
translation_en: Enlightened living souls who know that I am the master of all adhibhuta (material realm), adhidaiva (gods), and adhiyajna (Lord of sacrifices), remain completely in Me even at the time of death.
explanation_en: The chapter's closing image — remaining fixed on Krishna even at the moment of death, having understood him as the master of the material realm, the celestial realm, and all sacrifice — sets up exactly the question Arjuna will ask to open the next chapter: what actually happens at that final moment.

అధిభూతం చ కిం ప్రోక్తమధిదైవం కిముచ్యతే ।। 1 ।।', 'అధియజ్ఞః  కథం కోఽత్ర దేహేఽస్మిన్మధుసూదన ।
ప్రయాణకాలే చ కథం జ్ఞేయోఽసి నియతాత్మభిః ।। 2 ।।']
translation_en: Arjuna said: O Lord, what is Brahman (the Absolute Truth)? What is Adhyatma (Soul)? And what is karma? What is called adhibhuta? And who is called the supreme god? Who is Adhyajna in the body and how did he become Adhyajna? O Krishna, how is it possible for the strong-willed to know You at the time of death?
explanation_en: Arjuna asks Krishna to define the major ideas that have appeared in the teaching. He wants to know what Brahman, the inner self, and karma mean in this setting. The question shows a student seeking precision rather than relying on impressive religious vocabulary. It prepares the chapter to connect abstract terms with the practical concern of how one lives.

explanation_en: Arjuna continues by asking about the perishable world, the divine order, and the Lord of sacrifice in the body. sanskrit_sloka:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ ।
అక్షరం బ్రహ్మ పరమం స్వభావోఽధ్యాత్మముచ్యతే  ।
భూతభావోద్భవకరో  విసర్గః  కర్మసంజ్ఞితః  ।। 3 ।।
translation_en: Sri Bhagavan said: Brahman is the supreme, imperishable essence; The spirit of a person is called Adhyatma. Actions related to the material nature of living beings and their development are called karma or actions with fruition.
explanation_en: Krishna calls Brahman the imperishable supreme reality that does not pass away. He identifies adhyatma with the essential nature of the individual self. Karma here means the creative outgoing activity through which embodied beings arise. The verse therefore distinguishes eternal reality, personal identity, and the process of becoming.

sanskrit_sloka:
అధిభూతం క్షరో భావః పురుషశ్చాధిదైవతమ్ ।
అధియజ్ఞోఽహమేవాత్ర దేహే దేహభృతాం వర ।। 4 ।।
translation_en: This ever-changing physical creation is called adibhuta; Adhidaiva is the cosmic form of God who is the head of the gods in creation; I, who reside in the hearts of all demons, am known as Adhiyajna, i.e. Lord of all Yajnas.
explanation_en: Krishna describes adhibhuta as the changing field of material existence. Adhidaiva refers to the cosmic divine principle associated with embodied life. He then says that he himself is adhiyajna, the inner Lord of sacrifice in every body. The answer gathers cosmic process, divine governance, and inward presence into one framework.

sanskrit_sloka:

translation_en: Remembering Me at the time of death he who leaves the body reaches Me. There is no doubt about this.
explanation_en: Krishna says that one who departs the body remembering him reaches his state. The verse presents final awareness as spiritually consequential rather than accidental. It does not suggest that a last-minute thought can replace a whole life of formation. The next verses make clear that enduring remembrance is cultivated through ongoing practice.

Krishna is emphasizing the shaping power of habit, attention, and desire. This makes spiritual discipline a daily formation of consciousness, not an emergency strategy.

explanation_en: The mind reaches the Supreme Person through steady practice that does not wander elsewhere. A sustained inward orientation gradually becomes the path to the divine goal.

ఆదిత్యవర్ణం తమసః పరస్తాత్ ।। 9 ।।', 'ప్రయాణకాలే మనసాచలేన

explanation_en: The instruction begins with withdrawing the senses from their scattered outward movement. The mind is steadied in the heart while the life force is directed toward the head. ఓమిత్యేకాక్షరం బ్రహ్మ వ్యాహరన్మామనుస్మరన్  ।

sanskrit_sloka:
మాముపేత్య పునర్జన్మ దుఃఖాలయమశాశ్వతమ్  ।

explanation_en: Those who reach Krishna do not return to the temporary world marked by suffering. Krishna calls their attainment the highest fulfillment. sanskrit_sloka:
['యత్ర కాలే త్వనావృత్తిం ఆవృత్తిం చైవ యోగినః ।
ప్రయాతా యాంతి తం కాలం వక్ష్యామి భరతర్షభ ।। 23 ।।', 'అగ్నిర్జ్యోతిరహః శుక్లః షణ్మాసా ఉత్తరాయణమ్ ।
తత్ర ప్రయాతా గచ్ఛంతి బ్రహ్మ బ్రహ్మవిదో జనాః ।। 24 ।।', 'ధూమో రాత్రిస్తథా కృష్ణః షణ్మాసా దక్షిణాయనమ్ ।
తత్ర చాంద్రమసం జ్యోతిర్యోగీ ప్రాప్య నివర్తతే ।। 25 ।।', 'శుక్లకృష్ణే గతీ హ్యేతే జగతః శాశ్వతే మతే ।
ఏకయా యాత్యనావృత్తిమ్ అన్యయావర్తతే పునః ।। 26 ।।']
translation_en: I will now explain to you, O best of Bharatas, the various ways of passing away from this world, one of which leads to salvation and the other to rebirth. Those who know the Supreme Brahman and leave this world during the six months of Uttarayana, in Shukla Paksha, during the day, attain Parama Pada. Those who practice Vedic Karma Kandala, during Dakshinayana six months, during Krishna Paksha, during Dhumra period, at night, leave this world - attain heavenly worlds. After experiencing the pleasures of heaven, they come back to this earth. These two - bright and dark, paths always exist in this world. The bright path leads to salvation and the dark path to rebirth.
explanation_en: Krishna now introduces two enduring paths connected with departure from the world. One is associated with non-return, while the other leads back into return. He presents the distinction to instruct the yogi rather than to encourage anxiety about omens. The discussion will end by directing Arjuna back to constant yoga.

Those who know the Supreme Brahman and leave this world during the six months of Uttarayana, in Shukla Paksha, during the day, attain Parama Pada. Those who practice Vedic Karma Kandala, during Dakshinayana six months, during Krishna Paksha, during Dhumra period, at night, leave this world - attain heavenly worlds. Those who know the Supreme Brahman and leave this world during the six months of Uttarayana, in Shukla Paksha, during the day, attain Parama Pada. Those who practice Vedic Karma Kandala, during Dakshinayana six months, during Krishna Paksha, during Dhumra period, at night, leave this world - attain heavenly worlds. Those who practice Vedic Karma Kandala, during Dakshinayana six months, during Krishna Paksha, during Dhumra period, at night, leave this world - attain heavenly worlds. తస్మాత్ సర్వేషు కాలేషు యోగయుక్తో భవార్జున  ।। 27 ।।
translation_en: Yogis who know the secret of these two paths, O Partha, never fall prey to lust. Therefore, be sthitudavai (united with God) in yoga sarvada (at all times).
explanation_en: A yogi who understands these two paths is not confused by them. Knowledge here removes uncertainty about the differing outcomes Krishna has described. But Krishna does not leave Arjuna absorbed in speculation about departure. He returns to the central instruction to remain established in yoga at every time.

sanskrit_sloka:

దానేషు యత్పుణ్యఫలం ప్రదిష్టమ్ ।
అత్యేతి తత్సర్వమిదం విదిత్వా
యోగీ పరం స్థానముపైతి చాద్యమ్ ।। 28 ।।
translation_en: Yogis who know this secret - the practice of Vedic Karma Kandas, Vedadhyayana, performance of Yajnas, penance and charity - all these attain fruit beyond pious fruits. Such Yogis attain Parama Pada.
explanation_en: Understanding this teaching carries the yogi beyond the merit assigned to Vedic study, sacrifice, austerity, and giving. Krishna does not dismiss those practices, but he places the knowledge of yoga within a higher horizon. The result is attainment of the supreme and original abode. The chapter closes by presenting yoga as a path beyond accumulated religious reward toward lasting realization.

sanskrit_sloka:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ ।
ఇదం తు తే గుహ్యతమం ప్రవక్ష్యామ్యనసూయవే ।
జ్ఞానం విజ్ఞానసహితం యద్ జ్ఞాత్వా మోక్ష్యసేఽశుభాత్ ।। 1 ।।
translation_en: Sri Bhagavan said: O Arjuna, since you are not jealous of me, I will now tell you this most secret knowledge and empirical knowledge; After knowing this you will be freed from all material sufferings.
explanation_en: Krishna tells Arjuna that because he is free from envy, he can now hear the most confidential knowledge together with its deeper realization. This teaching concerns the nature of the Divine and how a person can reach the highest spiritual goal. It is not meant to remain as information but to be understood and experienced. Krishna therefore begins by preparing Arjuna for a more direct understanding of devotion.

sanskrit_sloka:
రాజవిద్యా రాజగుహ్యం పవిత్రమిదముత్తమమ్  ।
ప్రత్యక్ష్యావగమం ధర్మ్యం సుసుఖం కర్తుమవ్యయమ్ ।। 2 ।।
translation_en: This knowledge is the king of all learning and the most secret. It sanctifies those who hear it. It is directly experiential, virtuous, easy to practice, and gives lasting results.
explanation_en: Krishna calls this knowledge the king of all knowledge and the greatest of secrets because it is pure, directly realizable, consistent with dharma, and capable of producing a lasting result. It is not merely theoretical knowledge that remains separate from life. A person who follows it can experience its truth through practice. Its value lies in the transformation it brings.

sanskrit_sloka:
అశ్రద్దధానాః పురుషా ధర్మస్యాస్య  పరంతప ।
అప్రాప్య మాం  నివర్తంతే  మృత్యుసంసారవర్త్మని ।। 3 ।।
translation_en: People who have no faith in this Dharma, cannot attain Me, O conqueror of enemies. They repeatedly return to this world in the cycle of birth and death.
explanation_en: Krishna says that those who lack faith in this teaching do not reach him and continue within the cycle of birth and death. Faith is presented here as the willingness to trust and follow the path rather than simply hearing about it. Without that openness, the teaching cannot become a lived spiritual discipline. The result is continued attachment to material existence.

sanskrit_sloka:
మయా తతమిదం సర్వం జగదవ్యక్త మూర్తినా ।
మత్-స్థాని సర్వభూతాని న చాహం తేష్వవస్థితః ।। 4 ।।
translation_en: This entire universe is pervaded by My inmanifest form. All beings abide in Me but I abide in them.
explanation_en: Krishna says that his unmanifest form pervades the entire universe and that all beings exist within him, yet he is not confined by them. The Divine therefore supports everything without being limited to the visible forms of creation. This presents a relationship between the Supreme and the universe that cannot be reduced to ordinary physical containment. Krishna is both present throughout creation and beyond its limitations.

sanskrit_sloka:
న చ మత్ స్థాని భూతాని పశ్య మే యోగమైశ్వరమ్ ।
భూతభృన్న చ భూతస్థో మమాత్మా భూతభావనః ।। 5 ।।
translation_en: However, beings are not fixed in me. Behold the wonder of my divine power! Although I am the creator and administrator of all living beings, I am not affected by them or by material nature.
explanation_en: Krishna adds that, in another sense, beings do not remain within him in the ordinary way. He describes this apparent contradiction as a divine mystery: he sustains all beings while remaining beyond them. The verse prevents Arjuna from reducing the Supreme either to the visible universe or to something completely separate from it. The relationship between the Divine and creation is therefore deeper than ordinary categories can express.

sanskrit_sloka:
యథాకాశస్థితో నిత్యం వాయుః సర్వత్రగో మహాన్ ।
తథా సర్వాణి భూతాని మత్స్థానీత్యుపధారయ  ।। 6 ।।
translation_en: Even as the mighty wind that blows throughout, is always fixed in the sky, so all living beings are always fixed in Me.
explanation_en: Krishna compares this relationship to the wind moving within space. The wind exists in space without limiting or exhausting the space that supports it. In the same way, all beings exist within the Supreme without limiting the Supreme. The comparison gives Arjuna a simple way to approach an otherwise difficult spiritual idea.
word_by_word_meaning_en: yatha — however; akasa-sthitah — situated in the sky; nityam — always; vayuh — blowing wind; sarvatra-gah — blowing all over; mahan — of great power; tatha — in the same way; sarvani-bhutani — all living beings; mat-sthani — having settled in myself; iti — in this way; upadharaya — know.

sanskrit_sloka: ['సర్వభూతాని కౌంతేయ ప్రకృతిం యాంతి మామికామ్ ।\nకల్పక్షయే పునస్తాని కల్పాదౌ విసృజామ్యహమ్ ।। 7 ।।', 'ప్రకృతిం స్వామవష్టభ్య విసృజామి పునః పునః ।\nభూతగ్రామమిమం కృత్స్నమ్ అవశం ప్రకృతేర్వశాత్ ।। 8 ।।']
translation_en: At Kalpantara (at the end of a Kalpa), all beings merge into My primordial Prakriti Shakti. At the beginning of the next creation, O son of Kunti, I will manifest them again. Subduing my Prakriti (physical) energy, I am producing these innumerable living beings, according to their respective natures, again and again.
explanation_en: Krishna says that at the end of a cosmic cycle all beings enter into his material nature, and at the beginning of another cycle they emerge again. Creation and dissolution are therefore part of a recurring cosmic process. The forms of living beings change, but the divine principle behind the process remains. Krishna places the entire cycle within his higher control.

translation_en: At Kalpantara (at the end of a Kalpa), all beings merge into My primordial Prakriti Shakti. At the beginning of the next creation, O son of Kunti, I will manifest them again. Subduing my Prakriti (physical) energy, I am producing these innumerable living beings, according to their respective natures, again and again.
explanation_en: Krishna says that he repeatedly brings the multitude of beings into existence through his material nature. The forms of life appear according to the forces and qualities operating within that nature. Creation is therefore presented as an ordered process rather than as something independent of the Divine. Krishna remains the source behind the process without becoming bound by it.

sanskrit_sloka:
న చ మాం తాని కర్మాణి నిబధ్నంతి  ధనంజయ  ।
ఉదాసీనవదాసీనమసక్తం తేషు కర్మసు ।। 9 ।।
translation_en: O conqueror of riches, none of these deeds can bind me. As a neutral observer, I remain indifferent to any of these karmas.
explanation_en: Krishna says that these acts of creation do not bind him because he remains detached from them. Nature performs its work, but Krishna does not become attached to the results of that work. His example shows that action itself is not what creates bondage; attachment to action and its results does. This distinction is important for understanding how spiritual freedom is possible while activity continues.

sanskrit_sloka:
మయాధ్యక్షేణ ప్రకృతిః సూయతే సచరాచరమ్ ।
హేతునానేన కౌంతేయ జగద్విపరివర్తతే  ।। 10 ।।
translation_en: Acting under my direction, this material energy gives birth to all the material demons, O son of Kunti. For this reason, the physical world undergoes change (creation, state and rhythms).
explanation_en: Krishna says that material nature produces all moving and unmoving beings under his supervision. Nature carries out the visible process of creation, but it operates within a higher divine order. The universe therefore has both a material mechanism and a governing principle behind it. Krishna's role is not separate from nature's activity, yet he remains above its limitations.
word_by_word_meaning_en: maya — by me; Prasadena — direction; prakritiḥ — the physical physical force; suyate — is brought into being; sa — both; chara-achara — conscious-unconscious; hetuna — cause; anena — of this; Kaunteya — Arjuna, son of Kunti; jagat — in the material world; viparivartate — undergoing change.

sanskrit_sloka:
అవజానంతి మాం మూఢా  మానుషీం  తనుమాశ్రితమ్  ।
పరం  భావమజానంతో మమ భూతమహేశ్వరమ్  ।। 11 ।।
translation_en: When I incarnated in my human form, the fools could not recognize me. They do not know the divinity of My Personality who is Mahesvara to all demons.
explanation_en: Krishna says that people who fail to recognize his divine nature disregard him when he appears in human form. They see only the outward human appearance and miss the Supreme reality present through it. Their mistake comes from judging the Divine entirely through ordinary perception. The verse contrasts seeing Krishna's external form with recognizing who he truly is.
word_by_word_meaning_en: avajananti — negligent; mam — me; mudha — ignorant; manushim — man; tanum — form; ashritam — taken; param — divine; bhavam — personality; ajanantah — who do not know; mama — I; bhuta — to all living beings; Maheshwaram — Maheshvara.

sanskrit_sloka:
మోఘాశా మోఘకర్మాణో  మోఘజ్ఞానా విచేతసః  ।
రాక్షసీమాసురీం  చైవ ప్రకృతిం మోహినీం శ్రితాః ।। 12 ।।
translation_en: People who are deluded by physical magical power develop asuristic and atheistic sentiments. In that state of bewilderment, their hopes for progress/welfare are futile, all the karmas they perform with falsakti are futile and their knowledge is bewildered.
explanation_en: Those whose understanding is confused are described as having vain hopes, vain actions, and fruitless knowledge. Because their view of reality is distorted, their efforts remain directed toward limited or destructive purposes. The problem is therefore deeper than a single wrong action; it affects the way they understand life itself. Krishna contrasts this condition with the clear understanding of those who recognize the Divine.
word_by_word_meaning_en: mogha-ashah — having vain hopes; mogha-karmanah — those who perform useless deeds; mogha-jnana — possessed of confused knowledge; vichetasah — deluded; rakshaseem — demon; Asurim — Atheist; Cha — and; eva — surely; prakriti — physical energy; mohinem — bewitched; sritah — the refuge.

sanskrit_sloka:
మహాత్మానస్తు మాం పార్థ దైవీం ప్రకృతిమాశ్రితాః  ।
భజంత్యనన్యమనసో జ్ఞాత్వా భూతాదిమవ్యయమ్  ।। 13 ।।
translation_en: O Partha, the great souls who have taken refuge in my divine power will know that I, Sri Krishna, am the Supreme Being, the original source of all creation. With ananya chitta, they engage in my bhakti with their mind fixed on me alone.
explanation_en: Great souls, by contrast, take refuge in Krishna's divine nature and worship him with focused minds. They recognize him as the imperishable source of all beings rather than merely as an individual figure. Their devotion is supported by spiritual understanding, so knowledge and worship work together. Their entire orientation is directed toward the Supreme.

sanskrit_sloka:
సతతం కీర్తయంతో మాం యతంతశ్చ దృఢవ్రతాః  ।
నమస్యంతశ్చ మాం భక్త్యా నిత్యయుక్తా ఉపాసతే ।। 14 ।।
translation_en: Always chanting my divine leelas, practicing with firm determination, humbly bowing down before me, they constantly worship me with loving devotion.
explanation_en: Krishna describes his devotees as constantly glorifying him, striving with determination, bowing before him, and remaining devoted to him. Their remembrance is not limited to occasional religious practice but becomes a continuing part of their lives. Steady effort and worship keep their minds oriented toward the Divine. The verse emphasizes constancy as an important quality of devotion.
word_by_word_meaning_en: satatam — always; kirtayantaḥ — singing the glories of Bhagavat; mam — me; yatantah — laboring; Cha — and; dhrdhavratah — with determination; namasyantah — humbly bowing; Cha — and; mam — me; bhaktya — loving devotion; nitya-yukta — eternally united; upasate — worshiped.

sanskrit_sloka:
జ్ఞానయజ్ఞేన చాప్యన్యే  యజంతో  మాముపాసతే ।
ఏకత్వేన పృథక్త్వేన బహుధా విశ్వతోముఖమ్  ।। 15 ।।
translation_en: Others, engaged in the jnana samuparjana yajna, worship Me in many ways. Some see me as indistinctly united with them, while others regard me as separate from themselves. Yet some worship in the infinite manifestations of My cosmic form.
explanation_en: Some seekers worship Krishna through the sacrifice of knowledge, recognizing the one Supreme Reality through different expressions. Their approaches may differ in the way they understand and contemplate the Divine, yet their worship is still directed toward the highest reality. The verse therefore allows for different forms of spiritual contemplation. What gives them unity is the Supreme toward which their understanding is directed.
word_by_word_meaning_en: jnana-yajnena — the yajna of acquiring knowledge; Cha — and; anye — others; yajantah — is worshipped; mam — me; upasate — worshiped; ekattvena — with incomparable unity; prthaktvena — separately; bahudha — of various kinds; visvathah-mukham — cosmic form.

sanskrit_sloka: ['అహం క్రతురహం యజ్ఞః  స్వధాహమహమౌషధమ్ ।\nమంత్రోఽహమహమేవాజ్యమ్ అహమగ్నిరహం హుతమ్  ।। 16 ।।', 'పితాహమస్య జగతో మాతా ధాతా పితామహః ।\nవేద్యం పవిత్రమోంకార ఋక్సామ యజురేవ చ ।। 17 ।।']
translation_en: I am the Vedic kratu, I am the yajna and the offering to the patriarchs. I am the medicine, I am the Vedic mantra. I am the ghee, I am the fire, I am the offering. I am the father of this world. I am the mother and guardian of the world; I am the Father; I am the sanctifier; I am the goal of knowledge, the sacred sound Om Kara, I am the Rigveda, the Samaveda and the Yajurveda.
explanation_en: Krishna identifies himself with the entire structure of sacrifice: the ritual, the offering, the sacred ingredients, the fire, and the mantra. He also identifies himself as the father, mother, sustainer, and grandfather of the universe, as well as the object of knowledge. The teaching is that nothing essential to sacred practice stands outside the Supreme. Krishna is both present through the means of worship and the ultimate reality toward which worship is directed.

translation_en: I am the Vedic kratu, I am the yajna and the offering to the patriarchs. I am the medicine, I am the Vedic mantra. I am the ghee, I am the fire, I am the offering. I am the father of this world. I am the mother and guardian of the world; I am the Father; I am the sanctifier; I am the goal of knowledge, the sacred sound Om Kara, I am the Rigveda, the Samaveda and the Yajurveda.
explanation_en: Krishna describes himself as the father, mother, sustainer, and grandsire of the universe. The verse emphasizes that the many supports of spiritual life ultimately point back to Krishna.

sanskrit_sloka:
గతిర్భర్తా ప్రభుః సాక్షీ నివాసః శరణం సుహృత్ ।
ప్రభవః ప్రలయః స్థానం నిధానం బీజమవ్యయమ్  ।। 18 ।।
translation_en: I am the supreme goal of all demons, and I am their manager, lord, witness, abode, shelter and friend. I am the source, end, and basis of creation; I am the eternal place and the eternal seed.
explanation_en: Krishna identifies himself as the goal, supporter, Lord, witness, dwelling place, refuge, and friend. He is also the origin and dissolution of creation, its foundation, and its imperishable seed. These descriptions show the Divine as both the source from which existence arises and the reality in which it is sustained. Nothing in creation is independent of that sustaining presence.

sanskrit_sloka:
తపామ్యహమహం వర్షం నిగృహ్ణామ్యుత్సృజామి చ ।
అమృతం చైవ మృత్యుశ్చ సదసచ్చాహమర్జున  ।। 19 ।।
translation_en: I radiate heat in the form of the sun. I stop the rain and make it rain. I am immortal and I come in the form of death. O Arjuna, I am the eternal soul and also the temporary substance.
explanation_en: Krishna says that he gives heat, sends and withholds rain, and is both immortality and death. He is also described as being and non-being, encompassing what appear to be opposing aspects of existence. The changing processes of nature therefore remain within the larger reality of the Supreme. Krishna is not limited to only one side of experience.

sanskrit_sloka:
త్రైవిద్యా మాం  సోమపాః  పూతపాపా
యజ్ఞైరిష్ట్వా స్వర్గతిం ప్రార్థయంతే ।
తే పుణ్యమాసాద్య సురేంద్రలోకమ్
అశ్నంతి దివ్యాన్ దివి దేవభోగాన్ ।। 20 ।।
translation_en: Devotees to the Sakama rituals mentioned in the Vedas worship Me by performing Yajna sacrifices. By drinking Soma rasa, which is the remnant of Yajna, all the sins are gone and the pure ones hope to go to the heavenly worlds. As a result of their pious deeds, they go to the world of Lord Indra, and enjoy all the luxuries of the gods.
explanation_en: Those who follow Vedic rituals while seeking heavenly rewards can reach the celestial worlds through their sacrifices. They enjoy the results of their accumulated merit after reaching those higher realms. Yet the goal remains tied to a temporary reward rather than liberation. Krishna is beginning to distinguish heavenly enjoyment from lasting freedom.

sanskrit_sloka:
తే తం భుక్త్వా స్వర్గలోకం విశాలం
క్షీణే  పుణ్యే మర్త్యలోకం విశంతి ।
ఏవం త్రయీధర్మమనుప్రపన్నా
గతాగతం కామకామా లభంతే ।। 21 ।।
translation_en: They come back to the earth after all the fruits of their virtues have been consumed by enjoying the vast pleasures of the heavenly world. In this way, those who practice the Vedic Karma Kandas for the attainment of Bhoga Vastu, come and go again and again on earth.
explanation_en: When their accumulated merit is exhausted, those who reached heaven through ritual return to the mortal world. Their movement between higher and lower conditions continues because their actions were performed with a desire for results. The pleasure they gained is temporary because the merit supporting it eventually ends. Krishna contrasts this cycle with the lasting freedom associated with devotion to him.

sanskrit_sloka:
అనన్యాశ్చింతయంతో మాం యే జనాః  పర్యుపాసతే ।
తేషాం నిత్యాభియుక్తానాం యోగక్షేమం వహామ్యహమ్  ।।  22 ।।
translation_en: There are those who always remember Me and are engaged in exclusive devotion to Me, and to those whose mind is fixed on Me, I provide what they lack and preserve what they have.
explanation_en: Those who worship Krishna alone with unwavering devotion and constantly remember him are assured of what they need and the protection of what they possess. Their relationship with the Divine is based on complete devotion rather than the pursuit of a limited reward. Krishna presents himself as personally caring for such devotees. The verse expresses the security that comes from wholehearted dependence on the Divine.
word_by_word_meaning_en: ananyah — always; chintayantah — remembering; mam — me; ye — whoever; janah — the people; paryupasate — just worship (me); tesham — of them; nitya -abhiuktanam — who are always engaged in me; Yoga — bestows spiritual wealth; kshemam — protect the spiritual wealth; Vahami — carry; Aham — I.

sanskrit_sloka:
యేఽప్యన్యదేవతా  భక్తా  యజంతే శ్రద్ధయాన్వితాః  ।
తేఽపి మామేవ  కౌంతేయ  యజంత్యవిధిపూర్వకమ్  ।। 23 ।।
translation_en: O son of Kunti, I am also worshiped by those who diligently worship other gods. But, it seems they have done it in the wrong way.
explanation_en: Krishna says that even those who worship other deities with faith are ultimately worshipping him, although they do not understand the Supreme fully. Their sincerity is acknowledged, but their understanding of the highest reality remains incomplete. Because the object and purpose of their worship are limited, the results are also limited. The verse distinguishes sincere worship from complete spiritual understanding.

sanskrit_sloka:
మచ్చిత్తా మద్గతప్రాణా బోధయంతః పరస్పరమ్ ।
కథయంతశ్చ మాం నిత్యం తుష్యంతి చ రమంతి చ ।। 9 ।।
translation_en: My devotees are always satisfied with Me when their minds ascend to Me and their lives are surrendered to Me. Telling each other about Me and discussing My glories, they experience the greatest satisfaction and bliss.
explanation_en: The picture of devotees whose greatest joy comes from talking to each other about Krishna reframes devotion as something communal rather than solitary. Satisfaction here isn't found in private contemplation alone but explicitly in shared conversation — company as part of the practice, not a distraction from it.
word_by_word_meaning_en: mat-chittah — my mind ascended; mat-gata-pranah — having surrendered to Me; bodhayantah — instructing (with the divine knowledge of the Lord); mutual — to each other; kathayantah — tell; Cha — and; mam — about me; nityam — eternally; tusyanti — satisfaction; Cha — and; ramanti — (they) rejoice; Cha — and.

sanskrit_sloka:
తేషాం సతతయుక్తానాం భజతాం ప్రీతిపూర్వకమ్ ।
దదామి బుద్ధియోగం తం యేన మాముపయాంతి తే ।। 10 ।।
translation_en: To those whose mind is united with Me in loving devotion, I bestow divine knowledge by which they may attain Me.
explanation_en: The promise of 'divine knowledge' given specifically to those bound to Krishna in loving devotion suggests understanding isn't purely an intellectual achievement earned through study. It's described here as something granted in response to a particular quality of relationship, arriving as a kind of gift rather than an accomplishment.
word_by_word_meaning_en: tesham — to them; satata-yuktanam — always with strong will; bhajatam — for those engaged in devotion; preti-purukham — with love; dadami — I give; buddhi-yoga — divine knowledge; tam — that; yena — because of what; mam — to me; upayanti — comer; te — they.

sanskrit_sloka:
తేషామేవానుకంపార్థమ్ అహమజ్ఞానజం తమః
నాశయామ్యాత్మభావస్థొ జ్ఞానదీపేన భాస్వతా ।। 11 ।।
translation_en: With affection for them, I who am present in their hearts, will destroy the darkness created by ignorance with the bright lamp of knowledge.
explanation_en: The image of Krishna dwelling within the heart and personally dispelling the darkness of ignorance with 'the lamp of knowledge' makes this feel less like doctrine and more like intimate care. Compassion is named as the motive — not obligation, but affection driving the removal of confusion.
word_by_word_meaning_en: tesham — to them; eva — only; anukampa-artham — have mercy on me; Aham — I; ajnana-jam — born of ignorance; tamah — darkness; nasayami — destroys; atma-bhava — in their heart; sthah — residing; jnana — knowledge itself; dipena — with the lamp; bhasvata — shining.

sanskrit_sloka:
['అర్జున ఉవాచ ।
పరం బ్రహ్మ పరం ధామ పవిత్రం పరమం భవాన్ ।
పురుషం శాశ్వతం దివ్యమ్ ఆదిదేవమజం విభుమ్ ।। 12 ।।', 'ఆహుస్త్వామృషయః  సర్వే దేవర్షిర్నారదస్తథా ।
అసితో దేవలో వ్యాసః  స్వయం చైవ బ్రవీషి మే ।। 13 ।।']
translation_en: Arjuna said: Thou art the Parabrahma, the Parandham, the Supreme Holy One, the eternal God, the primordial man, the birthless and the supreme. Sages like Narada, Asita, Devala and Vyasa have declared this, and now you yourself are declaring this to me.
explanation_en: Arjuna's response is a cascade of superlatives — Supreme Brahman, eternal, primordial, birthless — piled up almost breathlessly, each title reaching for something beyond the last. It reads like someone trying to find language adequate to an experience that keeps exceeding whatever word they just used.
word_by_word_meaning_en: Arjunah Uvacha — Arjuna spoke; param — supreme; brahma — Brahman; param — supreme; dhama — abode; pavitra — who sanctifies; param — supreme; bhavan — you; purusha — male; स्वात्मा — eternal; divya — divine; adi-devam — of the primordial gods; ajam — birthless; vibhum — great/glorious; Ahuh — (they) declared; tvam — you; rishayah — the sages; Survey — All; deva-rishi-naradah — Devarshi Narada; tatha — and; asitah — asita; devalah — the Lord; vyasah — Vyasa; svayam — as self; Cha — and; eva — truly; bravishi — You yourself are declaring; May — to me.

sanskrit_sloka:
['అర్జున ఉవాచ ।
పరం బ్రహ్మ పరం ధామ పవిత్రం పరమం భవాన్ ।
పురుషం శాశ్వతం దివ్యమ్ ఆదిదేవమజం విభుమ్ ।। 12 ।।', 'ఆహుస్త్వామృషయః  సర్వే దేవర్షిర్నారదస్తథా ।
అసితో దేవలో వ్యాసః  స్వయం చైవ బ్రవీషి మే ।। 13 ।।']
translation_en: Arjuna said: Thou art the Parabrahma, the Parandham, the Supreme Holy One, the eternal God, the primordial man, the birthless and the supreme. Sages like Narada, Asita, Devala and Vyasa have declared this, and now you yourself are declaring this to me.
explanation_en: Arjuna backs his own declaration with authority beyond himself, citing sages like Narada and Vyasa who've said the same thing before him, and now hearing it confirmed directly from Krishna. He's building a case, not just expressing feeling — tradition and direct testimony reinforcing each other.

sanskrit_sloka:
సర్వమేతదృతం మన్యే యన్మాం వదసి కేశవ ।
న హి తే భగవన్ వ్యక్తిం విదుర్దేవా న దానవాః  ।। 14 ।।
translation_en: O Krishna, I believe with firm faith that everything you have said is true.  O Lord, neither the gods nor the demons can know your real form.
explanation_en: Declaring firm faith that everything Krishna has said is true, while adding that not even the demons can know his real form, Arjuna draws a sharp line: acceptance here isn't naive, it's made with awareness of exactly how hard this truth is to grasp, which makes the trust more significant, not less.

sanskrit_sloka:
స్వయమేవాత్మనాత్మానం వేత్థ త్వం పురుషోత్తమ ।
భూతభావన భూతేశ దేవదేవ జగత్పతే ।। 15 ।।
translation_en: O Purushottam, Creator of all things, Sarvabhutesa, Devdeva, Jagatpathe! In fact, you only know yourself through your own transcendental power.
explanation_en: Arjuna's observation that Krishna can only be known through his own power — that no external effort from anyone else could reach him — is a striking admission of limits. Even devoted, sincere inquiry, Arjuna seems to recognize, ultimately depends on Krishna's own self-revealing, not on the seeker's effort alone.
word_by_word_meaning_en: svayam — as thyself; eva — truly; atmana — by yourself; Atmanam — You; vetha — will be known; tvam — you; purusha-uttama — the Supreme Supreme Purusha; bhuta-bhavana — who created all the demons; bhutesa — Lord of all; deva-deva — God of the gods; Jagat-pathe — Lord of the world.

sanskrit_sloka: ['వక్తుమర్హస్యశేషేణ దివ్యా హ్యాత్మవిభూతయః ।\nయాభిర్విభూతిభిర్లోకాన్ ఇమాంస్త్వం వ్యాప్య తిష్ఠసి ।। 16 ।।', 'కథం విద్యామహం యోగిన్ త్వాం సదా పరిచింతయన్ ।\nకేషు కేషు చ భావేషు చింత్యోఽసి భగవన్మయా ।। 17 ।।']
translation_en: Please explain to me Your Divine Vibhutas in which You pervade and reside in all the worlds. O Yogeshwara, how can I know and remember You? And in what forms can I contemplate You, O Lord, while meditating?
explanation_en: Arjuna's request to hear the divine manifestations in detail — how Krishna pervades the worlds, how he might be remembered in meditation — shifts from praise into a practical, almost logistical question: given everything just said, what does someone actually do with it?
word_by_word_meaning_en: vakhtum — to explain; arhasi — please; aseshena — completely; divyaḥ — divine; hi — truly; atma — thine own; vibhutayah — of the vibhutas; yabhih — cured by what; vibhutibhih — the vibhutis; lokan — in all the worlds; Iman — these; tvam — you; vyapya — spreading; tishtasi — being steady;  katha — in any way; Vidyam aham — how can I know; Yogin — the head of Yogamaya; tvam — you; sada — always;  parichintayan — meditating; keshu — of what; keshu — of what; Cha — and; bhavesu — in forms; chintyah asi — to be remembered; Bhagavan — Param Divya Mangala Swarupa; Maya — by me.

sanskrit_sloka: ['వక్తుమర్హస్యశేషేణ దివ్యా హ్యాత్మవిభూతయః ।\nయాభిర్విభూతిభిర్లోకాన్ ఇమాంస్త్వం వ్యాప్య తిష్ఠసి ।। 16 ।।', 'కథం విద్యామహం యోగిన్ త్వాం సదా పరిచింతయన్ ।\nకేషు కేషు చ భావేషు చింత్యోఽసి భగవన్మయా ।। 17 ।।']
translation_en: Please explain to me Your Divine Vibhutas in which You pervade and reside in all the worlds. O Yogeshwara, how can I know and remember You? And in what forms can I contemplate You, O Lord, while meditating?
explanation_en: The repeated request echoes the previous verse almost word for word, and the repetition itself carries meaning: Arjuna isn't satisfied with abstraction. He wants specifics he can actually hold onto and return to, not a single sweeping statement he might forget.
