sanskrit_sloka:
విస్తరేణాత్మనో యోగం విభూతిం చ జనార్ధన ।
భూయః కథయ తృప్తిర్హి  శృణ్వతో నాస్తి మేఽమృతమ్  ।। 18 ।।
translation_en: Again recount Your divine glories and incarnations in abundance, O Janardhana.  If you listen to your nectar, it will never fade away.
explanation_en: Arjuna's plea to hear it 'again, in abundance,' comparing the teaching to nectar that never grows old no matter how often tasted, gives real texture to his eagerness. This isn't dutiful listening — he's describing something he genuinely can't get enough of.
word_by_word_meaning_en: vistarena — widely;  atmanah — of you; yoga — divine glories;  vibhutim — vibhuti (qualities/riches); Cha — and;  Janardhana — Lord Krishna, the well-being of the people;  bhuyah — again;  kathaya — explain; trptih — satisfaction; hi — because; srinvatah — while listening;  na asti — does not exist; may — to me;  Amritham — nectar.

sanskrit_sloka:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ ।
హంత తే కథయిష్యామి దివ్యా హ్యత్మవిభూతయః ।
ప్రాధాన్యతః కురుశ్రేష్ఠ నాస్త్యంతో విస్తరస్య మే ।। 19 ।।
translation_en: Sri Bhagavanu said: Now I will briefly explain to you, O great son, my divine visions, for there is no end to their description.
explanation_en: Krishna's agreement to explain, tempered by the caveat that there's no end to the full description, sets honest expectations before the list even begins: what follows will be illustrative, not exhaustive. He's choosing highlights, not attempting completeness.
word_by_word_meaning_en: Sri -bhagavan-uvacha — Sri Bhagavan Palikenu; Hanta — OK; te — to you; kathaishyami — I explain; divyaḥ — divine; hi — truly; atma-vibhutayah — my divine vibhutas; பர்ரியாயாயா — the main; kurushrestha — the best among Kuru clansmen; na, asti — no; antah — the end; vastarasya — vast glories; May — mine.

sanskrit_sloka:
అహమాత్మా గుడాకేశ సర్వభూతాశయస్థితః ।
అహమాదిశ్చ మధ్యం చ భూతానామంత ఏవ చ ।। 20 ।।
translation_en: O Arjuna, I am seated in the hearts of all demons. I am the beginning, middle and end of all beings.
explanation_en: Naming himself as the Self within every being's heart, and as the beginning, middle, and end of all things, gives the coming catalog its foundation — before listing specific examples across nature, Krishna first states the underlying principle they're all going to illustrate: his presence isn't external decoration on things, it's their core.
word_by_word_meaning_en: Aham — I; atma — soul; Gudakesha — Arjuna, conqueror of sleep; sarva-bhuta — of all the demons; ashaya-sthitah — seated in the heart; Aham — I; adih — beginning; Cha — and; Madhyam — middle; Cha — and; bhutanam — of all the bhutams; antah — final (end); eva — also; Cha — and.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఆదిత్యానామహం విష్ణుః జ్యోతిషాం రవిరంశుమాన్ ।
మరీచిర్మరుతామస్మి  నక్షత్రాణామహం శశీ ।। 21 ।।
translation_en: Of Aditi's twelve sons I am Vishnu; I am the sun among bright things. I am the moon among the stars of the night sky and the maruthu among the maruts.
explanation_en: Choosing Vishnu among Aditi's sons and the sun among luminous things picks, in each category, the example most associated with supreme brightness or centrality. The pattern that will run through this whole list starts here: not just any instance, but the pinnacle within each domain.
word_by_word_meaning_en: adityanam — among the twelve sons of Aditi; Aham — I; Vishnuh — the form of Vishnu; Jyotisham — in bright objects; ravih — the sun; anshu-man — bright; marichih — forgotten; marutham — among the Maruts; asmi — I; nakshatraana — in the stars; Aham — I; Sasih — the moon.

sanskrit_sloka:
వేదానాం సామవేదోఽస్మి దేవానామస్మి వాసవః ।
ఇంద్రియాణాం మనశ్చాస్మి  భూతానామస్మి చేతనా ।। 22 ।।
translation_en: I am Sama Veda among the Vedas, Indra among the gods. the mind in the senses; Consciousness in animals.
explanation_en: Naming the Sama Veda among scriptures and the mind among the senses picks two very different kinds of things — one a body of sacred text, the other a faculty of perception — and treats them by the same logic: whatever holds the position of essence or refinement within its category represents him best.
word_by_word_meaning_en: vedanam — in the Vedas; sama-vedah — the sama veda; asmi — I; devanam — among the deities; asmi — I; vasavah — Indra; indriyanam — in the senses; manah — the mind; Cha — and; asmi — I; bhutanam — among creatures; asmi — I; Chetana — consciousness.

sanskrit_sloka:
రుద్రాణాం శంకరశ్చాస్మి విత్తేశో యక్షరక్షసామ్ ।
వసూనాం పావకశ్చాస్మి మేరుః శిఖరిణామహమ్ ।। 23 ।।
translation_en: Among the Rudras I am Shankara; Kubera is among the Asuras; Agni is among the Vasus and Meru is among the mountains.
explanation_en: Shankara among the Rudras, Kubera among wealth-holding spirits, Agni among the Vasus — this string of specific mythological figures may read as obscure detail, but the underlying claim is consistent: within every class of divine being, there's a representative point where Krishna's presence concentrates most visibly.
word_by_word_meaning_en: rudranam — among the Rudras; Shankarah — Shiva (Lord Shankara); Cha — and; asmi — I; vitta-esah — goddess of wealth and treasurer of the gods; yaksha — the yakshas; rakshasam — among the demons; vasunam — in the sums; pavakah — fire; Cha — and; asmi — I; meruh — Mount Meru; shikharinam — in the mountains; Aham — I.

sanskrit_sloka:
పురోధసాం చ ముఖ్యం మాం విద్ధి పార్థ బృహస్పతిమ్ ।
సేనానీనామహం స్కందః సరసామస్మి సాగరః ।। 24 ।।
translation_en: Among the priests I am Jupiter; Among soldiers I am Karthike; And in the reservoirs know that I am the ocean.
explanation_en: Naming Brihaspati among priests and the ocean among bodies of water pairs a human role with a natural feature, showing the list isn't confined to mythology — it reaches into professions and geography alike, suggesting no category of existence is exempt from having its own point of maximal expression.
word_by_word_meaning_en: purodhasam — among the priests; Cha — and; important — chiefs; mam — I; viddhi — know; Partha — Arjuna, O son of Pritha; brihaspatim — Jupiter; senaninam — among the generals; Aham — I; skandah — Kartikeya; sarasam — in reservoirs; asmi — I; sagarah — ocean.

sanskrit_sloka:
మహార్షీణాం భృగురహం గిరామస్మ్యేకమక్షరమ్ ।
యజ్ఞానాం జపయజ్ఞోఽస్మి స్థావరాణాం హిమాలయః ।। 25 ।।
translation_en: I am Bhrigu Maharshi among sages and 'Om' is the transcendental of sounds. I am chanting the Lord's name again and again in japas (sacrifices); I am the Himalayas among the settlements;
explanation_en: Bhrigu among sages and Om among sounds sit side by side here — a person renowned for wisdom and a syllable considered the root of all sacred utterance. Krishna is drawing a line from embodied excellence to the very sound believed to underlie creation itself.
word_by_word_meaning_en: maha-risinam — among the sages; bhriguh — sage Bhrigu; Aham — I; giram — in words (mantra); Ekam Aksharam — the monosyllabic 'Om'; yajnanam — in the yajnas; japayajnah — the yajna of constantly chanting the names of the Lord with devotion; asmi — I am; ஶாலையாந்தானானை — in the bases (of the immovable); Himalayah — Himalayas.

sanskrit_sloka:
అశ్వత్థః సర్వవృక్షాణాం దేవర్షీణాం చ నారదః ।
గంధర్వాణాం చిత్రరథః సిద్ధానాం కపిలో మునిః ।। 26 ।।
translation_en: Among the trees I am the Ravi tree; Narada is among the gods. Among the Gandharvas I am Chitrarathu, among the Siddhas I am Kapila Muni.
explanation_en: The list turns briefly to plant and mythic-being life — a particular sacred tree, a celestial musician, a renowned sage among the perfected beings — extending the scope of the catalog into realms most people rarely think to include in ideas about the divine.
word_by_word_meaning_en: asvatthah — the Ravi tree; sarva-vrikshanam — among all the trees; deva-risinam — among the gods; Cha — and; naradah — Narada; gandharvanam — among the Gandharvas; chitrarathah — the charioteer; siddhanam — among all siddhas; Kapilah Munih — Kapila Muni.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఉచ్చైఃశ్రవసమశ్వానాం విద్ధి మామమృతోద్భవమ్ ।
ఐరావతం గజేంద్రాణాం నరాణాం చ నరాధిపమ్ ।। 27 ।।
translation_en: Amongst the horses, I, born of the Amrita Samudra, am Uchchaihsravasam. Among the Gajendras I am Airavata and the king of men.
explanation_en: Uchchaihshravas, the legendary horse born from the churning of the ocean, and Airavata, the great elephant, both carry mythic weight as symbols of power and nobility. Choosing them over ordinary horses or elephants keeps the pattern consistent: the extraordinary example within a category, not the average one.

explanation_en: Naming himself Ananta among serpents and Varuna among water-dwelling beings, Krishna's list keeps threading through categories that might seem far removed from ordinary spiritual concern — reptiles, aquatic life — reinforcing that nothing is too minor or strange to be included.

sanskrit_sloka:
ప్రహ్లాదశ్చాస్మి దైత్యానాం కాలః కలయతామహమ్ ।

sanskrit_sloka:

sanskrit_sloka:
మృత్యుః సర్వహరశ్చాహమ్ ఉద్భవశ్చ భవిష్యతామ్ ।

translation_en: I am the all-consuming death, I am the producer of all that is to come.  In female characteristics I am fame, wealth, fine speech, memory, intelligence, courage and forgiveness.
explanation_en: All-consuming death and the source of what's yet to arise sit together in one verse, capturing both ends of existence at once — the force that ends things and the origin of things not yet born. The list of feminine qualities that follows — fame, memory, forgiveness — extends this same logic into the register of virtue itself.

sanskrit_sloka:
బృహత్సామ తథా సామ్నాం గాయత్రీ ఛందసామహమ్ ।

explanation_en: Naming himself as specific meters, months, and seasons — the Gayatri among poetic meters, spring among seasons — grounds the abstract claim of omnipresence in the concrete rhythm of ritual calendars and natural cycles that would have structured daily and religious life.

explanation_en: Claiming to be victory among the victorious and virtue among the righteous, and even gambling among forms of trickery, is a startling inclusion — Krishna doesn't exempt ambiguous or ethically loaded activities from the list. Even competitive cunning, in its own domain, is claimed as an expression of his presence.

బహూన్యదృష్టపూర్వాణి పశ్యాశ్చర్యాణి భారత ।। 6 ।।
translation_en: See in me, O descendant of Bharata, (twelve) sons of Aditi, (eight) Vasus, (eleven) Rudras, (two) sons of Ashwini, besides, (forty-nine) Maruts and many other wonders which have not been performed before.
explanation_en: Krishna tells Arjuna to behold the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Ashvins, Maruts, and many other wonders never seen before. The universal form contains the various divine powers and orders known through the Vedic tradition. Arjuna is not being shown one isolated deity but the whole range of cosmic manifestation together. The vision will therefore exceed anything he has previously encountered.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఇహైకస్థం జగత్ కృత్స్నం పశ్యాద్య సచరాచరమ్ ।
మమ దేహే గుడాకేశ యచ్చాన్యద్ద్రష్టుమిచ్ఛసి ।। 7 ।।
translation_en: O Arjuna, see now the world in which all beings are gathered together, in my cosmic form. And if you want to see anything else, see them all in my universe form.
explanation_en: Krishna tells Arjuna to see the entire universe, with everything moving and unmoving, gathered together in his form. Whatever else Arjuna wishes to see is also present there. The universal form contains the whole field of existence rather than one limited part of it. Past, present, and future are revealed within this extraordinary vision.

sanskrit_sloka:
న తు మాం శక్యసే ద్రష్టుమనేనైవ  స్వచక్షుషా  ।
దివ్యం దదామి తే చక్షుః పశ్య మే యోగమైశ్వరమ్  ।। 8 ।।
translation_en: But, you cannot see my cosmic form with your natural eyes. Therefore, I grant you divine vision. Behold my great glory.
explanation_en: Krishna tells Arjuna that his ordinary eyes cannot see the universal form. He therefore grants Arjuna divine sight so that he can behold Krishna's supreme power. The vision requires a capacity beyond ordinary physical perception. What follows is possible only through Krishna's grace.

sanskrit_sloka:
సంజయ ఉవాచ ।
ఏవముక్త్వా తతో రాజన్ మహాయోగేశ్వరో హరిః ।
దర్శయామాస పార్థాయ పరమం రూపమైశ్వరమ్ ।। 9 ।।
translation_en: Sanjaya said: O Maharaja, Pidapa who spoke thus, that Yogeshvara Sri Krishna, showed Arjuna His divine and glorious form.
explanation_en: Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra that, after speaking these words, Krishna revealed his supreme divine form to Arjuna. He describes Krishna as the great Lord of Yoga who is now displaying his extraordinary majesty. Because of Vyasa's gift of divine sight, Sanjaya is able to witness the vision as well. He now begins describing what Arjuna saw.

sanskrit_sloka: ['అనేకవక్త్రనయనమ్ అనేకాద్భుతదర్శనమ్ ।\nఅనేకదివ్యాభరణం దివ్యానేకోద్యతాయుధమ్ ।। 10 ।।', 'దివ్యమాల్యాంబరధరం దివ్యగంధానులేపనమ్ ।\nసర్వాశ్చర్యమయం దేవమనంతం విశ్వతోముఖం ।। 11 ।।']
translation_en: In its cosmic form, Arjuna saw infinite faces and eyes. They have many divine ornaments and many kinds of divine weapons. The form has many garlands on its body and is fragrant with divine fragrance. Sarvatra manifests Himself with His face as the great infinite Ishvara.
explanation_en: Arjuna sees the universal form with countless faces and eyes and innumerable wondrous sights. It is adorned with divine ornaments and carries many divine weapons. The form is decorated with celestial garlands and garments and filled with divine fragrance. Every direction is occupied by this vast and astonishing presence.

sanskrit_sloka: ['అనేకవక్త్రనయనమ్ అనేకాద్భుతదర్శనమ్ ।\nఅనేకదివ్యాభరణం దివ్యానేకోద్యతాయుధమ్ ।। 10 ।।', 'దివ్యమాల్యాంబరధరం దివ్యగంధానులేపనమ్ ।\nసర్వాశ్చర్యమయం దేవమనంతం విశ్వతోముఖం ।। 11 ।।']

explanation_en: The universal form appears radiant with heavenly ornaments, garlands, garments, and fragrances. It has countless faces turned in every direction and seems to contain an immeasurable variety of divine beauty. The vision is not simply enormous but completely beyond ordinary experience. Its magnificence overwhelms the limits of Arjuna's normal perception.

sanskrit_sloka:
దివి సూర్య సహస్రస్య భవేద్యుగపదుత్థితా ।
యది భాః సదృశీ సా స్యాత్ భాసస్తస్య మహాత్మనః ।। 12 ।।
translation_en: Even a thousand suns shining in the sky at the same time cannot match the brilliance of that supreme form.
explanation_en: If the brilliance of a thousand suns were to rise together in the sky, it might resemble the splendor of that universal form. The comparison is meant to give some sense of a radiance beyond ordinary measure. Even such an image cannot fully capture what Arjuna is seeing. The vision expresses divine majesty on a cosmic scale.

sanskrit_sloka:
తత్రైకస్థం జగత్ కృత్స్నం ప్రవిభక్తమనేకధా ।
అపశ్యద్దేవదేవస్య  శరీరే పాండవస్తదా ।। 13 ।।
translation_en: There, in the body of that god, Arjuna saw that all the universes were in one place.
explanation_en: Arjuna sees the entire universe, with its many divisions and countless beings, gathered within Krishna's universal form. What normally appears scattered across space is present together before him. The separate worlds and beings are revealed as parts of one immense divine reality. The vision makes the unity underlying creation directly visible.

sanskrit_sloka:
తతః స విస్మయావిష్టో హృష్టరోమా ధనంజయః ।
ప్రణమ్య శిరసా దేవం కృతాంజలిరభాషత ।। 14 ।।
translation_en: Then Arjuna, who was overwhelmed with paramascharya and his hair was matted, bowed his head with folded hands and praised the Lord in this way.
explanation_en: Arjuna is overwhelmed with wonder and bows his head before Krishna with folded hands. The vision has moved him beyond ordinary confidence and familiarity. He recognizes that he is standing before a reality far greater than the human form he knew. His response naturally becomes reverence, awe, and surrender.

అర్జున ఉవాచ ।
పశ్యామి దేవాంస్తవ దేవ దేహే
సర్వాంస్తథా భూతవిశేషసంఘాన్
బ్రహ్మాణమీశం కమలాసనస్థమ్
ఋషీంశ్చ సర్వానురగాంశ్చ దివ్యాన్ ।। 15 ।।
translation_en: Arjuna said, O Sri Krishna, in your body I see - all the gods, many crores of living beings, Lord Brahma seated on a lotus, Lord Shiva, all the sages, and the divine serpents.
explanation_en: Arjuna sees within Krishna's universal form the gods, different classes of beings, Brahma seated on the lotus, sages, and divine serpents. Everything he once understood as separate is now visible within one cosmic body. The vision includes both the highest divine beings and the many orders of creation. Krishna's form therefore appears as the container of the entire spiritual and material hierarchy.
word_by_word_meaning_en: Arjuna Uvacha — Arjuna spoke; పశ్యామి — దర్శించితిని; దేవాన్ — సర్వ దేవతలను; తవ — నీ; deva — the Lord; దేహే — శరీరము యందే; sarvan — everything; tatha — and; భూత విశేష-సంఘాన్ — విశేషమైన ప్రాణిసమూహమును; బ్రహ్మాణo — బ్రహ్మ దేవుడు; isam — Lord Siva; కమల-ఆసన-స్థం —  తామర పూవు యందు కూర్చుని ఉన్న; rishim — the sages; Cha — and; sarvan — all; Uragon — Serpents; Cha — and; దివ్యాన్ — దివ్యమైన.

sanskrit_sloka:
అనేకబాహూదరవక్త్రనేత్రం
పశ్యామి త్వాం సర్వతోఽనంతరూపమ్  ।
నాంతం న మధ్యం న పునస్తవాదిం
పశ్యామి విశ్వేశ్వర విశ్వరూప  ।। 16 ।।
translation_en: I see in all directions Your infinite forms with innumerable arms, bellies, faces and eyes. O Vishvesvara, the universe is your embodiment, I do not see any primordial changes in you.
explanation_en: Arjuna sees countless arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes extending without apparent end. He cannot find the beginning, middle, or end of this universal form. Its vastness extends in every direction and overwhelms his ordinary sense of space. The vision makes the limitless nature of Krishna unmistakable.

sanskrit_sloka:
కిరీటినం గదినం చక్రిణం చ
తేజోరాశిం సర్వతో దీప్తిమంతమ్
పశ్యామి త్వాం దుర్నిరీక్ష్యం సమంతాత్
దీప్తానలార్క ద్యుతిమప్రమేయమ్  ।। 17 ।।
translation_en: I see your all-shining form, crowned and armed with chakra-gada weapons. It is difficult to see you because of your radiance like the sun that spreads fire in all directions.
explanation_en: Arjuna sees Krishna's form shining with crowns, clubs, discs, and blazing radiance. The brilliance is so intense that it seems impossible to look upon directly. He recognizes Krishna as a vast, luminous reality beyond ordinary measurement. The divine form combines beauty, power, and overwhelming light.

sanskrit_sloka:
త్వమక్షరం పరమం వేదితవ్యం
త్వమస్య విశ్వస్య పరం నిధానమ్
త్వమవ్యయః శాశ్వతధర్మగోప్తా
సనాతనస్త్వం పురుషో మతో మే ।। 18 ।।
translation_en: I have come to know that You are the imperishable Supreme Lord, the Supreme Truth propounded by the Vedas. You are the foundation of all creation; You are the eternal protector of Sanatana Dharma; You are the Eternal Supreme Lord.
explanation_en: Arjuna declares Krishna to be the imperishable Supreme, the ultimate reality to be known. He recognizes Krishna as the foundation of the entire universe and the protector of the eternal order. He sees Krishna as the ancient Divine Person and the everlasting source of spiritual existence. The vision has confirmed in direct experience what Krishna had taught earlier.

అనంతబాహుం  శశిసూర్యనేత్రమ్  ।
పశ్యామి త్వాం దీప్తహుతాశవక్త్రం
స్వతేజసా విశ్వమిదం తపంతమ్  ।। 19 ।।
translation_en: Thou art without beginning-middle-end; Your powers are limitless. You have infinite arms; Sun and moon are like your eyes and fire is like your mouth. I behold Thee, Who warmest all creation with Thy radiance.
explanation_en: Arjuna sees Krishna without beginning, middle, or end, possessing limitless power and innumerable arms. He sees the sun and moon as the eyes of the cosmic form and blazing fire emerging from its mouths. The immense radiance of the form seems to illuminate the entire universe. Arjuna recognizes this as the Supreme reality whose power fills all existence.

sanskrit_sloka:
ద్యావాపృథివ్యోరిదమంతరం హి
వ్యాప్తం త్వయైకేన దిశశ్చ సర్వాః ।
దృష్ట్వాద్భుతం రూపముగ్రం తవేదం
లోకత్రయం ప్రవ్యథితం మహాత్మన్ ।। 20 ।।
translation_en: You are pervading all the middle space from Devi to Bhuvi and also in all directions.  O Mahatma, beholding Your glorious and terrifying form, I observe that even the thorns tremble with fear.
explanation_en: Arjuna says that the space between heaven and earth and all directions are filled by Krishna's presence. The sight of this extraordinary form has left the worlds shaken and amazed. Nothing appears to stand outside the universal body. The vision reveals a Divine presence that completely encompasses creation.
word_by_word_meaning_en: dyau-a-prthivyo — from Devi to Bhuvi; Itam — of this; Antaram — throughout the middle space; hi — truly; spread — spread out; tvaya — by you; ekena — alone; dishah — in the directions; Cha — and; sarvah — all; drishtva — seeing; awesome — awesome; rupam — form; ugram — furious; tava — of you; This — this; loka — the worlds; triad — three; pravyathitam — trembling; Maha-Atman — Mahatmuda.

అమీ హి త్వాం  సురసంఘా విశంతి
కేచిద్భీతాః  ప్రాంజలయో గృణంతి ।
స్వస్తీత్యుక్త్వా  మహర్షిసిద్ధసంఘాః
స్తువంతి త్వాం స్తుతిభిః  పుష్కలాభిః  ।। 21 ।।
translation_en: All the gods are entering into you and taking shelter of you. Some are fearfully glorifying you with folded hands. Sages and Siddhas praise you with auspicious hymns and hymns.
explanation_en: Arjuna sees the hosts of gods entering Krishna's form, some approaching with reverence and folded hands. Great sages and perfected beings praise Krishna with hymns of glory. Others stand astonished, overwhelmed by the majesty of what they see. The universal form inspires worship, wonder, and fear even among exalted beings.

sanskrit_sloka:

విశ్వేఽశ్వినౌ మరుతశ్చోష్మపాశ్చ ।
గంధర్వయక్షాసురసిద్ధసంఘా
వీక్షంతే త్వాం విస్మితాశ్చైవ సర్వే ।। 22 ।।
translation_en: The Rudras, the Adityas, the Vasus, the Sadhyas, the Visvadevatas, the sons of the Ashwinis, the Maruts, the Pitras, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, ​​the Asuras and the Siddhas all gaze upon You with awe.
explanation_en: Arjuna sees the Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Vishvedevas, Ashvins, Maruts, ancestors, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and Siddhas gathered within the universal form. Some are amazed, while others are overcome by fear. The entire range of divine, ancestral, celestial, and powerful beings is present before him. The vision reveals that all these orders exist within Krishna's greater reality.

sanskrit_sloka:
రూపం మహత్తే బహువక్త్రనేత్రం
మహాబాహో బహుబాహూరుపాదమ్ ।
బహూదరం బహుదంష్ట్రాకరాళం

explanation_en: Arjuna says that Krishna's immense form, with countless faces, eyes, arms, legs, bellies, and terrible mouths, has shaken him and the worlds. Arjuna admits that the sight fills him with both wonder and terror.

explanation_en: Arjuna says that the universal form reaches the heavens and shines with many colors and open mouths. Its blazing eyes and terrible appearance leave him deeply disturbed. He cannot find steadiness or peace while looking upon it. The vision has become so immense that Arjuna no longer knows how to relate to what he sees.

గరీయసే బ్రహ్మణోఽప్యాదికర్త్రే  ।
అనంత దేవేశ జగన్నివాస
త్వమక్షరం సదసత్  తత్పరం యత్ ।। 37 ।।
translation_en: O Mahatma, why should not even those superior to Brahma, the original creator, prostrate before you? O Ananthu, O Lord of the Gods, O Shelter of the world, You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
explanation_en: Arjuna asks how anyone could fail to bow before Krishna, who is greater than Brahma and the original creator. He recognizes Krishna as the Supreme, the imperishable reality beyond both being and non-being. He sees Krishna as the source of the universe and the highest object of worship. His words show that the earlier uncertainty about Krishna's true nature has disappeared.

త్వమస్య విశ్వస్య పరం నిధానమ్
వేత్తాసి వేద్యం చ పరం చ ధామ
త్వయా తతం విశ్వమనంతరూప ।। 38 ।।
translation_en: Thou art the eternal God and the primordial God; You are the only support and refuge for the entire universe. You are the All-Knowing and the One to be known. You are Parandham. O Anantarupa, you are the one who pervades the entire universe.
explanation_en: Arjuna declares Krishna to be the primal Divine Person, the oldest reality, and the supreme foundation of the universe. He sees Krishna as both the knower and the object of knowledge and as the highest spiritual destination. The entire universe is pervaded by this eternal reality. Arjuna is now describing Krishna in the highest theological language available to him.

sanskrit_sloka:

ప్రజాప్రతిస్త్వం ప్రపితామహశ్చ ।
నమో నమస్తేఽస్తు సహస్రకృత్వః
పునశ్చ భూయోఽపి నమో నమస్తే ।। 39 ।।
translation_en: You are the Lord of Air, the Lord of Yamadharma, the Lord of Fire, the Lord of Varuna and the Moon. You are the creator Brahma and the father of all demons. I bow to you thousands of times, I bow again and again.
explanation_en: Arjuna identifies Krishna with Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, the moon, Prajapati, and the ancient ancestor. He is recognizing the many divine powers as expressions of the one Supreme Lord. His repeated salutations show that he no longer sees Krishna as merely one figure among many. Everything worthy of reverence is being gathered into Krishna.

explanation_en: Arjuna offers Krishna salutations from the front, behind, and from every direction. Because Krishna pervades everything, there is no direction in which he is absent. Arjuna bows to the immeasurable Lord whose power is beyond his ability to comprehend. The universal vision has turned his relationship with Krishna into complete reverence.

మయా ప్రమాదాత్ ప్రణయేన వాపి ।। 41 ।।', 'యచ్చావహాసార్థమసత్కృతోఽసి
విహారశయ్యాసనభోజనేషు ।
ఏకోఽథ వాప్యచ్యుత తత్సమక్షం
తత్ క్షామయే త్వామహమప్రమేయమ్ ।। 42 ।।']
translation_en: Thinking that you are my sakhud (friend), I called you "O Krishna", "O Yadava", "O my dear friend" with great joy. Not knowing your majesty, I behaved carelessly and excessively. While playing, while resting, while sitting, while eating, while alone or in the presence of others, if I have behaved rudely towards you, even as a joke, I apologize for that.
explanation_en: Arjuna asks Krishna to forgive him for having previously addressed him casually as a friend. He remembers calling Krishna 'O Krishna,' 'O Yadava,' or 'my friend' without understanding his supreme greatness. He now sees that the familiar human form had concealed a reality far beyond ordinary friendship. His apology comes from the humility produced by direct realization.

translation_en: You are the father of the entire universe and all living beings.  You are the supreme worshiper and the supreme spiritual guru. O one of unequaled power, when you have no equal in the heavens, who can surpass you?
explanation_en: Arjuna declares that Krishna is the father of the entire world, the moving and unmoving. He is the teacher and the most worshipful reality, with no equal anywhere. Arjuna therefore asks Krishna for forgiveness and mercy. The universal vision has replaced familiarity with profound reverence.

The request combines humility with the intimacy of a personal relationship. He asks Krishna to forgive everything done through ignorance or affection.

translation_en: Pidapa, seeing your cosmic form which I have never seen before, I feel blissful. However, my mind was trembling with fear. Please have mercy on me and show me again your pleasing form, O Lord God, O Giver of refuge to the world.
explanation_en: Arjuna says that he is delighted to have seen something never seen before, yet he is also shaken with fear. He therefore asks Krishna to show him again a more reassuring form. The universal vision has fulfilled his desire for knowledge but has also overwhelmed him. He now longs to see Krishna in a form his heart can approach peacefully.

explanation_en: Arjuna asks Krishna to appear again with a crown, mace, and discus, in the familiar divine form he can recognize. He wants to see the four-armed form rather than the terrifying cosmic manifestation. The request shows that Arjuna is seeking a form in which reverence and affection can exist together. He wants Krishna's divine presence without the overwhelming terror of the universal form.

explanation_en: Krishna says that, out of grace, he has shown Arjuna this supreme universal form through his own divine power. It is a form filled with brilliance, unlimited, primordial, and never before seen by Arjuna. The vision was not produced by ordinary spiritual effort alone. Krishna emphasizes that it was granted through divine grace.

explanation_en: Krishna says that this universal form cannot be seen merely through Vedic study, sacrifice, charity, rituals, or severe austerity. Those practices have their place, but they cannot by themselves produce this direct vision. The universal form is therefore not something that can be obtained simply by accumulating religious merit. It is revealed through a higher divine favor.

explanation_en: Krishna tells Arjuna not to be frightened or bewildered by what he has seen. He asks him to let go of his fear and become inwardly peaceful. The terrible cosmic vision was meant to reveal truth, not to leave Arjuna in despair. Krishna is now preparing to restore the reassuring form Arjuna requested.

explanation_en: Sanjaya says that Krishna then withdrew the universal form and appeared again in his gentle, familiar form. Seeing Krishna in this reassuring appearance, Arjuna's mind became calm and he returned to his normal state. explanation_en: Arjuna says that after seeing Krishna's gentle human form again, his mind has become calm and he has returned to his natural state. The fear produced by the universal vision has subsided. He can now relate to Krishna again without being overwhelmed by the cosmic manifestation. The familiar form restores his peace.

['శ్రీ భగవానువాచ ।
సుదుర్దర్శమిదం రూపం దృష్టవానసి యన్మమ ।
దేవా అప్యస్య రూపస్య నిత్యం దర్శనకాంక్షిణః ।। 52 ।।', 'నాహం వేదైర్న తపసా న దానేన న చేజ్యయా ।
శక్య ఏవంవిధో ద్రష్టుం దృష్టవానసి మాం యథా ।। 53 ।।']
translation_en: Sri Bhagavan said: It is very rare to see the form of Me that you see.  Even the gods wish to see it. Not by Vedadhyayana, not by penances, not by charity or by Yajnas, I do not appear as you have seen so far.
explanation_en: Krishna says that the form Arjuna has just seen is very difficult even for the gods to behold. The vision is therefore not an ordinary experience available to everyone. Even celestial beings long to see it. Its rarity emphasizes the extraordinary grace Arjuna has received.

explanation_en: Krishna says that the universal form cannot be seen through the Vedas, austerity, charity, or sacrifice alone. These practices by themselves cannot produce the direct vision Arjuna has received. The revelation therefore depends on something beyond ordinary spiritual effort. Krishna is pointing toward the necessity of divine grace and devotion.

sanskrit_sloka:
భక్త్యా త్వనన్యయా శక్య అహమేవంవిధోఽర్జున ।
జ్ఞాతుం ద్రష్టుం చ తత్వేన ప్రవేష్టుం చ పరంతప ।। 54 ।।
translation_en: O Arjuna, only by unalloyed devotion can I truly know myself standing before you. O Parantapa, thus having obtained my divine vision Pidapa may attain the state of unity with Me.
explanation_en: Krishna says that only through single-minded devotion can he be truly known, seen, and entered into as he really is. Devotion here is not merely an emotion but an undivided orientation toward Krishna. It allows the seeker to know the Divine beyond concepts and outward forms. Through such devotion, Krishna becomes directly accessible.

sanskrit_sloka:
మత్కర్మకృన్మత్పరమో మద్భక్తః సంగవర్జితః ।
నిర్వైరః సర్వభూతేషు యః స మామేతి పాండవ ।। 55 ।।
translation_en: Those who do all karmas for Me, depend on Me and are devoted to Me, free from selfishness, free from animosity towards all demons, such devotees will surely reach Me.
explanation_en: One who acts for Krishna, makes him the highest goal, remains devoted, gives up attachment, and bears no hatred toward any being reaches Krishna. The verse brings together action, devotion, renunciation, and universal goodwill. The goal is not withdrawal from life but acting without selfish attachment while keeping Krishna at the center. Krishna closes the chapter by presenting this integrated devotion as the path to him.
word_by_word_meaning_en: mat-karma-krit — performing duties for My sake; mat-paramah — regarding Me as the Supreme; mat-bhaktah — being my devotee; sanga varjitah — giving up material interests; nirvairah — without resentment; sarva-bhuteshu — to all the demons; yah — whoever; sah — he; mam — me; yeti — gets; Pandava — O Arjuna, son of the Pandava king.

sanskrit_sloka:
అర్జున ఉవాచ ।
ఏవం సతత యుక్తా యే భక్త్యాస్త్వాం పర్యుపాసతే ।
యే చాప్యక్షరమవ్యక్తం తేషాం కే యోగవిత్తమాః ।। 1 ।।
translation_en: Arjuna asked: Those who are always devoted to your embodied form and those who worship the formless Brahman - of these two types, who do you consider to be more excellent in yoga?
explanation_en: Arjuna asks which of the two is considered superior in yoga: those who worship Krishna with devotion in his personal form, or those who meditate on the imperishable, unmanifest Brahman. After witnessing the universal form, he now wants to understand the difference between these two ways of approaching the Divine. His question recognizes both personal devotion and meditation on the formless Absolute as serious spiritual paths. He wants Krishna to clarify which approach is considered the higher form of yoga.
word_by_word_meaning_en: Arjuna Uvacha — Arjuna spoke; evam — thus; satata — constantly; yukta — with devotion; ye — whoever; bhaktah — devotees; tvam — you; paryupasate — who worship; ye — they; Cha — and; api — also; Akshara — imperishable; avyaktam — formless Brahman; tesham — they; ke — who?; Yoga-with-tamah — Most excellent in yoga.

sanskrit_sloka:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ ।
మయ్యావేశ్య మనో యే మాం నిత్యయుక్తా ఉపాసతే ।
శ్రద్ధయా పరాయోపేతాస్తే మే యుక్తతమా మతాః ।। 2 ।।
translation_en: Sri Bhagavan said: I consider those who have fixed their minds on Me and are constantly engaged in devotion to Me with firm faith, to be the best yogis.
explanation_en: Krishna says that those who fix their minds on him and worship him with steady faith are considered the most perfectly united with him in yoga. Their attention is directed toward Krishna personally rather than toward an unmanifest reality. Faith and constant absorption are presented together, making devotion a matter of sustained inner commitment rather than occasional worship. Krishna's answer therefore gives personal devotion the clearest position in this comparison.
word_by_word_meaning_en: Sri-bhagavan-uvacha — Sri Bhagavan Palikenu; mai — in me; avesya — preoccupied; manah — the mind; ye — whoever; mam — me; nitya yuktah — always having ascendant; upasate — one who worships/worships; shraddhaya — with shraddha-beliefs; paraya — the best; upetah — having; te — they; may — by me; yukta-tamah — as being at a higher level in yoga; Matah — I think.

sanskrit_sloka: ['యే త్వక్షరమనిర్దేశ్యమవ్యక్తం పర్యుపాసతే ।\nసర్వత్రగమచింత్యం చ కూటస్థమచలం ధ్రువమ్  ।। 3 ।।', 'సన్నియమ్యేంద్రియగ్రామం సర్వత్ర  సమబుద్దయః ।\nతే ప్రాప్నువంతి మామేవ సర్వభూతహితే రతాః ।। 4 ।।']
translation_en: Those who worship the Formless Tattva of the Supreme Truth - imperishable, indefinable, immanent, all-pervading, beyond the senses, changeless, eternal and immovable - restraining the senses, being omniscient and engaged in the welfare of all beings - attain Me.
explanation_en: Krishna says that those who worship the imperishable, unmanifest, all-pervading, unthinkable, unchanging, and immovable Brahman also reach the Supreme. These seekers approach the Divine without relying on a perceivable personal form. The many descriptions in this verse emphasize a reality that cannot be grasped through ordinary sensory experience. Krishna therefore acknowledges the impersonal path as genuine even while distinguishing it from the devotional path.

sanskrit_sloka: ['యే త్వక్షరమనిర్దేశ్యమవ్యక్తం పర్యుపాసతే ।\nసర్వత్రగమచింత్యం చ కూటస్థమచలం ధ్రువమ్  ।। 3 ।।', 'సన్నియమ్యేంద్రియగ్రామం సర్వత్ర  సమబుద్దయః ।\nతే ప్రాప్నువంతి మామేవ సర్వభూతహితే రతాః ।। 4 ।।']
translation_en: Those who worship the Formless Tattva of the Supreme Truth - imperishable, indefinable, immanent, all-pervading, beyond the senses, changeless, eternal and immovable - restraining the senses, being omniscient and engaged in the welfare of all beings - attain Me.
explanation_en: Those who follow the unmanifest path control their senses, remain equal-minded in all situations, and devote themselves to the welfare of every living being. Their spiritual discipline requires both inner restraint and an attitude of equality toward the world around them. The path is therefore not simply intellectual meditation; it also demands disciplined conduct and concern for others. Krishna presents these qualities as essential to those who seek the imperishable through this approach.

sanskrit_sloka:
క్లేశోఽధికతరస్తేషామ్ అవ్యక్తాసక్తచేతసామ్ ।।
అవ్యక్తా హి గతిర్దుఃఖం దేహవద్భిరవాప్యతే ।। 5 ।।
translation_en: For those interested in the immanence of the mind, the path of Siddhi is fraught with difficulties. Worshiping the immanent is very difficult for material beings.
explanation_en: Krishna says that those whose minds are fixed on the unmanifest face greater difficulty because embodied beings find it hard to approach a goal that cannot be perceived through form. The challenge comes from the natural tendency of the mind to work through concrete objects and experiences. The impersonal path therefore demands a level of concentration and abstraction that is difficult for most embodied people. This explains why Krishna considers personal devotion the more accessible approach.

sanskrit_sloka: ['యే తు సర్వాణి కర్మాణి మయి సన్న్యస్య మత్పరః  ।\nఅనన్యేనైవ యోగేన మాం ధ్యాయంత ఉపాసతే ।। 6 ।।', 'తేషామహం సముద్ధర్తా మృత్యుసంసారసాగరాత్ ।\nభవామి నచిరాత్ పార్థ  మయ్యావేశితచేతసామ్ ।। 7 ।।']
translation_en: But those who dedicate all their deeds to Me, regard Me as the supreme goal, worship Me and meditate on Me with unalloyed devotion, O Partha, I will quickly liberate them from this ocean of mortals, as if their innermost being is united with Me.
explanation_en: Krishna describes those who dedicate all their actions to him, regard him as their supreme goal, and worship him with undivided devotion. Their relationship with Krishna extends beyond meditation into everything they do. By offering their actions to him, they turn ordinary responsibilities into part of their spiritual practice. The verse presents devotion as a way of organizing one's entire life around the Divine.

sanskrit_sloka: ['యే తు సర్వాణి కర్మాణి మయి సన్న్యస్య మత్పరః  ।\nఅనన్యేనైవ యోగేన మాం ధ్యాయంత ఉపాసతే ।। 6 ।।', 'తేషామహం సముద్ధర్తా మృత్యుసంసారసాగరాత్ ।\nభవామి నచిరాత్ పార్థ  మయ్యావేశితచేతసామ్ ।। 7 ।।']
translation_en: But those who dedicate all their deeds to Me, regard Me as the supreme goal, worship Me and meditate on Me with unalloyed devotion, O Partha, I will quickly liberate them from this ocean of mortals, as if their innermost being is united with Me.
explanation_en: Krishna promises to become the deliverer of those whose minds remain fixed on him, carrying them beyond the ocean of birth and death. The image of an ocean expresses the difficulty and vastness of the cycle from which the devotee seeks freedom. Krishna is not merely described as the goal of the journey but as the one who helps the devotee cross it. This gives the path of devotion a strong emphasis on divine grace and protection.

sanskrit_sloka:
మయ్యేవ మన ఆధత్స్వ మయి బుద్ధిం నివేశయ ।
నివసిష్యసి మయ్యేవ అత ఊర్ధ్వం న సంశయః ।। 8 ।।
translation_en: Fix your mind on me and offer your mind to me. After that, you will always reside in me. No doubt about it.
explanation_en: Krishna tells Arjuna to fix his mind on him and place his intellect in him, promising that by doing so Arjuna will live in him without doubt. The instruction involves both feeling and understanding, since the mind must remain devoted while the intellect also accepts Krishna as its highest focus. Spiritual absorption is therefore not presented as an occasional thought but as a complete orientation of consciousness. Krishna gives Arjuna the clearest form of the devotional practice before offering alternatives for those who find it difficult.
word_by_word_meaning_en: mai — on me; eva — only; manah — the mind; adhatsva — ascendant; mai — mine; buddhim — intellect; nivesya — offered/surrendered; nivasishyasi — You always reside; mai — in me; eva — only; atah urdhvam — and after that; na samsayah — no doubt.

sanskrit_sloka:
అథ చిత్తం సమాధాతుం న శక్నోషి మయి స్థిరమ్  ।
అభ్యాసయోగేన తతో మామిచ్ఛాప్తుం ధనంజయ ।। 9 ।।
translation_en: If you cannot fix the mind on Me, O Arjuna, practice remembering Me with devotion, restraining the mind from worldly matters.
explanation_en: If Arjuna cannot keep his mind steadily fixed on Krishna, Krishna tells him to practice bringing it back to him through disciplined spiritual effort. The mind may wander, but repeated practice gradually strengthens the ability to remain focused. This makes devotion something that can be developed through steady training rather than something that depends entirely on natural ability. Krishna therefore gives practice as the next step for a seeker who cannot yet remain constantly absorbed.
word_by_word_meaning_en: atha — if; chittam — mind; samadhatum — to ascend; na shaknoshi — if you are not able (cannot); mai — in me; sishtam — still; praya-yogena — united with the Lord through constant effort (practice); tatah — then; mam — me; iccha — desire; aptum — to get; Dhananjaya — Arjuna, conqueror of Siri's riches.

sanskrit_sloka:
అభ్యాసేఽప్యసమర్థోఽసి మత్కర్మపరమో భవ ।
మదర్థమపి కర్మాణి కుర్వన్ సిద్ధిమవాప్స్యసి ।। 10 ।।
translation_en: If you cannot practice remembering Me with devotion, try to do things for Me. By performing devotional service in this way, you can attain perfection.
explanation_en: If Arjuna is unable to follow even this practice, Krishna tells him to perform his actions for his sake. The emphasis now moves from controlling the mind directly to changing the purpose behind one's actions. Ordinary work can become spiritual practice when it is consciously performed as service to Krishna. This gives a practical way for devotion to enter daily life even when constant meditation is difficult.
word_by_word_meaning_en: practice — in practice; api — if; Asamartha — inability (inability); asi — you; mat-karma-paramah — work for Me with devotion; bhava — be; mat-artham — for my sake; api — also; karmani — karmas; kurvan — practice; siddhim — siddhi (perfection); avaapsyasi — you can get.

sanskrit_sloka:
అథైతదప్యశక్తోఽసి  కర్తుం మద్యోగమాశ్రితః  ।
సర్వకర్మఫలత్యాగం  తతః  కురు యతాత్మవాన్ ।। 11 ।।
translation_en: If you cannot work for Me with devotion, try to renounce the fruits of your karma and be steady in spirit.
explanation_en: If Arjuna cannot dedicate his actions to Krishna in this way, Krishna advises him to renounce attachment to the fruits of his actions. He can continue to perform his duties while giving up the demand that the results must turn out according to his expectations. This separates responsible action from the anxiety and possessiveness that often accompany its results. The teaching therefore provides another practical step toward freedom when the higher forms of practice are difficult.
word_by_word_meaning_en: atha — if; etat — this; api — also; Ashakta: — if unable (unable to do); asi — you; kartum — working; mad-yoga — with devotion to Me; ashritah — resorted to;  sarva-karma — of all karma (of all deeds); phala-tyagam — fruit sacrifice; tatah — then; kuru — do; yata-atma-van — the state of the soul itself.

sanskrit_sloka:
శ్రేయో హి జ్ఞానమభ్యాసాత్ జ్ఞానాద్ధ్యానం విశిష్యతే ।
ధ్యానాత్ కర్మఫలత్యాగః త్యాగాచ్ఛాంతిరనంతరమ్ ।। 12 ।।
translation_en: Knowledge is better than mechanical learning; Meditation is better than knowledge. Sacrifice for the fruit of karma is better than meditation, because peace is attained immediately after such a sacrifice.
explanation_en: Krishna says that knowledge is better than mere practice, meditation is better than knowledge, and renunciation of the fruits of action is better than meditation. When attachment to the results of action is truly given up, peace follows. The verse places inner freedom from results at the heart of spiritual progress. It shows that the quality of one's relationship with action matters as much as the practice itself.

sanskrit_sloka: ['అద్వేష్టా సర్వభూతానాం మైత్రః కరుణ ఏవ చ ।\nనిర్మమో నిరహంకారః సమదుఃఖసుఖః క్షమీ ।। 13 ।।', 'సంతుష్టః సతతం యోగీ  యతాత్మా దృఢనిశ్చయః ।\nమయ్యర్పితమనోబుద్ధిర్యో మధ్భక్తః  స మే ప్రియాః ।। 14 ।।']
translation_en: Those devotees who are non-hatred, friendly and compassionate towards all living beings are very dear to me. They are unattached/uninterested in property/money and without ego, equal in both happiness and sorrow and ever forgiving. They are always united with Me with contentment, devotion, self-restraint, strong will and offering mind to Me.
explanation_en: Krishna begins describing the qualities of a devotee who is dear to him. Such a person has no hatred toward any living being and instead is friendly and compassionate, while remaining free from possessiveness and excessive ego. He stays balanced in happiness and distress rather than allowing either to control him. Devotion is therefore shown not only through worship but through the way a person relates to every other being.

translation_en: Those devotees who are non-hatred, friendly and compassionate towards all living beings are very dear to me. They are unattached/uninterested in property/money and without ego, equal in both happiness and sorrow and ever forgiving. They are always united with Me with contentment, devotion, self-restraint, strong will and offering mind to Me.
explanation_en: The devotee is forgiving, content, self-controlled, firmly determined, and constantly devoted to Krishna. His mind and intellect remain fixed on the Divine instead of being pulled constantly in different directions. Contentment and determination give his devotion stability rather than allowing it to depend on changing circumstances. These qualities describe a person whose spiritual commitment has become part of his character.

sanskrit_sloka:
యస్మాన్నోద్విజతే లోకో లోకాన్నోద్విజతే చ యః ।
హర్షామర్షభయోద్వేగైః  ముక్తో యః స చ మే ప్రియ: ।। 15 ।।
translation_en: My devotees are very dear to me who do not cause pain (trouble) to anyone in the world and who are not agitated by anyone, who remain one in pleasures and pains, and who are free from fear and anxiety.
explanation_en: Krishna says that the devotee who does not disturb others and is not easily disturbed by others is dear to him. Such a person is free from excessive joy, envy, fear, and anxiety, so his inner state is not constantly controlled by what happens around him. At the same time, his own conduct does not become a source of unnecessary trouble for others. The verse connects devotion with both inner composure and harmlessness in one's dealings with the world.

sanskrit_sloka:
అనపేక్షః  శుచిర్దక్ష ఉదాసీనో గతవ్యథః ।
సర్వారంభపరిత్యాగీ యో మద్భక్తః స మే ప్రియః ।। 16 ।।
translation_en: My devotees who are disinterested in worldly gains, outwardly chaste, efficient, dispassionate, free from disturbance and unselfish in all affairs are very dear to Me.
explanation_en: The devotee is described as unattached, pure, capable, free from unnecessary dependence on results, and not overwhelmed by anxiety while performing actions. He continues to act responsibly without becoming emotionally controlled by the outcome. This combination of competence and detachment distinguishes spiritual action from both restless striving and passive withdrawal. Krishna presents such steadiness as a quality of one who is dear to him.

sanskrit_sloka:
యో న హృష్యతి న ద్వేష్టి న శోచతి న కాంక్షతి ।
శుభాశుభపరిత్యాగీ భక్తిమాన్యః స మే ప్రియః ।। 17 ।।
translation_en: Those who do not enjoy worldly pleasures and do not suffer from worldly miseries, who do not suffer loss or strive for gain, who renounce both good and bad deeds, such people, full of devotion, are very dear to me.
explanation_en: The devotee neither becomes excessively joyful nor sinks into sorrow, neither laments nor is driven by desire, and gives up attachment to favorable and unfavorable outcomes. His emotional state is no longer determined by whether circumstances happen to please him. This does not mean that he becomes indifferent, but that his devotion remains steady through changing experiences. Such freedom from emotional extremes is another sign of inner equanimity.

sanskrit_sloka: ['సమః శత్రౌ చ మిత్రే చ తథా మానాపమానయోః ।\nశీతోష్ణసుఖదుఃఖేషు సమః సంగవివర్జితః ।। 18 ।।', 'తుల్యనిందాస్తుతిర్మౌనీ సంతుష్టో యేన కేనచిత్ ।\nఅనికేతః స్థిరమతిర్భక్తిమాన్ మే ప్రియో నరః ।। 19 ।।']
translation_en: He who is equal to friends and foes, indifferent to honor and dishonor, equal to heat and cold, to pleasure and pain, and shuns evil company; Those who take insult and praise alike, who meditate in silence, who are content with what they have, who are uninterested in abode, whose mind is fixed on Me, who are filled with devotion to Me, such persons are very dear to Me.
explanation_en: Krishna says that the devotee remains equal toward friend and enemy and treats honor and dishonor, heat and cold, pleasure and pain alike. He does not allow social approval, physical discomfort, or emotional opposites to determine his inner stability. This equality extends across relationships, circumstances, and personal experiences. The verse shows how deeply detachment has become established in the devotee's way of life.

sanskrit_sloka: ['సమః శత్రౌ చ మిత్రే చ తథా మానాపమానయోః ।\nశీతోష్ణసుఖదుఃఖేషు సమః సంగవివర్జితః ।। 18 ।।', 'తుల్యనిందాస్తుతిర్మౌనీ సంతుష్టో యేన కేనచిత్ ।\nఅనికేతః స్థిరమతిర్భక్తిమాన్ మే ప్రియో నరః ।। 19 ।।']
translation_en: He who is equal to friends and foes, indifferent to honor and dishonor, equal to heat and cold, to pleasure and pain, and shuns evil company; Those who take insult and praise alike, who meditate in silence, who are content with what they have, who are uninterested in abode, whose mind is fixed on Me, who are filled with devotion to Me, such persons are very dear to Me.
explanation_en: The devotee is steady in praise and blame, content with what comes naturally, inwardly quiet, and free from excessive attachment to possessions or circumstances. He does not depend on the approval of others to maintain his sense of direction. His mind remains settled in Krishna even when the outside world responds differently to him. These qualities complete the portrait of the devotee whose inner life is governed by devotion rather than external conditions.

sanskrit_sloka:
యే తు ధర్మ్యామృతమిదం  యథోక్తం పర్యుపాసతే ।
శ్రద్ధధానా  మత్పరమా భక్తాస్తేఽతీవ మే ప్రియాః ।। 20 ।।
translation_en: Those who respect this Gnanamrita declared here and have faith in Me and devotion to Me as the ultimate goal, they are dearest to Me.
explanation_en: Krishna concludes that those who faithfully follow this immortal path of devotion and accept him as their supreme goal are especially dear to him. The qualities described throughout the chapter are not separate ideals but expressions of a life centered on the Divine. Compassion, equality, self-control, contentment, and freedom from attachment all support the devotee's steady relationship with Krishna. The chapter therefore ends by bringing its teaching back to unwavering faith and devotion as the highest goal.

sanskrit_sloka:
అర్జున ఉవాచ ।
ప్రకృతిం పురుషం చైవ క్షేత్రం క్షేత్రజ్ఞమేవ చ ।
ఏతద్వేదితుమిచ్ఛామి జ్ఞానం జ్ఞేయం చ కేశవ ।। 1 ।। *1
translation_en: Arjuna said, "O Kesava, what is Prakriti and Purusha, what is Kshetra and Ksetrajna? I want to know. What is true knowledge and what is the goal of such knowledge?"
explanation_en: Arjuna's cluster of questions — Prakriti, Purusha, the field, the knower of the field — shows him reaching for a more technical vocabulary than before, as if sensing that the emotional and devotional language of earlier chapters needs a more precise conceptual scaffolding underneath it to actually hold.

sanskrit_sloka:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ ।
ఇదం శరీరం కౌంతేయ క్షేత్రమిత్యభిధీయతే ।
ఏతద్యో వేత్తి తం ప్రాహుః  క్షేత్రజ్ఞ ఇతి తద్విదః ।। 2 ।।
translation_en: The Supreme Divine Lord spoke thus: O Arjuna, this body is the field, and that which is known about this body is the kshetrajna - both of which have been said by sages well versed.
explanation_en: Calling the body itself 'the field' and awareness of it 'the knower of the field' reframes the whole person as two distinct things co-existing rather than one unified self. It's a deceptively simple move that will structure everything else in the chapter: you are not your field, you are what knows it.

sanskrit_sloka:
క్షేత్రజ్ఞం చాపి మాం విద్ధి సర్వక్షేత్రేషు భారత ।
క్షేత్రక్షేత్రజ్ఞయోః జ్ఞానం యత్తద్ జ్ఞానం మతం మమ  ।। 3 ।।
translation_en: O descendant of Bharata, I am also the one who has reached every field. To know that this body is the kshetra (place of activity) and that the soul and the divine are kshetrajnas (pervaders of the field) is what I consider true knowledge.
explanation_en: Krishna's claim to be present as the knower in every field, not just in Arjuna's, universalizes the concept immediately — this isn't a private insight about one person's psychology, it's presented as the same underlying awareness operating identically in every body everywhere.

sanskrit_sloka:
తత్ క్షేత్రం యచ్చ యాదృక్చయద్వికారి యతశ్చ యత్ ।
స చ యో యత్ప్రభావశ్చ తత్సమాసేన మే శృణు ।। 4 ।।
translation_en: Listen, I will explain to you what the field is and its nature. I will also explain how the change occurs in it, what it is created by, who the Kshetrajna is and what is his power.
explanation_en: Promising to explain the field's nature, its changes, its origin, and the knower's power lays out an agenda with real structure — Krishna signals this won't be a single aphorism but a systematic unpacking, verse by verse, of a genuinely layered topic.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఋషిభిర్బహుధా గీతం ఛందోభిర్వివిధైః  పృథక్ ।
బ్రహ్మసూత్రపదైశ్చైవ హేతుమద్భిర్వినిశ్చితైః ।। 5 ।।
translation_en: The great sages have explained the truth about Kshetra and Kshetrajna in many ways. It is also stated in many Vedic mantras, especially in the Brahma Sutras where it is reasonably and conclusively stated.
explanation_en: By citing sages and the Brahma Sutras as prior sources for this teaching, Krishna positions himself as continuing an established inquiry rather than introducing something entirely new — grounding the coming explanation in a lineage of thought Arjuna would have already had some awareness of.

sanskrit_sloka:
మహాభూతాన్యహంకారో బుద్ధిరవ్యక్తమేవ చ ।
ఇంద్రియాణి దశైకం చ పంచ చేంద్రియగోచరాః ।। 6 ।।
translation_en: Its field consists of the five great demons, the ego, the intellect, the immanent nature, the eleven senses (the five sense organs, the five karmandriyas, the mind), and the five sense objects.
explanation_en: The inventory of the field's components — elements, ego, intellect, the senses and their objects — reads almost like a parts list, breaking the seemingly unified experience of being a person into discrete, analyzable pieces, each of which belongs to the field rather than to the one aware of it.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఇచ్ఛా ద్వేషః సుఖం దుఃఖం సంఘాతశ్చేతనా ధృతిః ।
ఏతత్ క్షేత్రం సమాసేన సవికారముదాహృతమ్ ।। 7 ।।
translation_en: Desire and hatred, happiness and sorrow, body, consciousness, mental force - all these together are called kshetra and its changes (vikaramula).
explanation_en: Adding desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, and even consciousness itself to what counts as part of the field pushes the boundary further than expected — even mental and emotional experience, not just the physical body, gets classified here as something observed rather than something the observer fundamentally is.

sanskrit_sloka:

ఆచార్యోపాసనం శౌచం స్థైర్యమాత్మవినిగ్రహః ।। 8 ।।', 'ఇంద్రియార్థేషు వైరాగ్యమనహంకార ఏవ చ ।

నిత్యం చ సమచిత్తత్వమ్ ఇష్టానిష్టోపపత్తిషు  ।। 10 ।।', 'మయి చానన్యయోగేన భక్తిరవ్యభిచారిణీ ।

అనాదిమత్పరం బ్రహ్మ న సత్తన్నాసదుచ్యతే ।। 13 ।।
translation_en: That which must be known, I will now tell you, after knowing it, one becomes immortal. That is the eternal Brahman which is beyond sat and asat.
explanation_en: Introducing what must be known to attain immortality — the eternal Brahman, beyond both being and non-being — signals a shift from ethical character to metaphysical reality. Having described the knower's qualities, Krishna now turns to what that knower ultimately comes to know.

సర్వతః శ్రుతిమల్లోకే సర్వమావృత్య తిష్ఠతి ।। 14 ।।
translation_en: Everywhere are His feet, eyes, heads and faces. His ears are also in all places, for He pervades the whole world.
explanation_en: Describing Brahman as having feet, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere, and ears in all places, uses deliberately embodied language for something explicitly beyond ordinary form — the paradox is intentional, gesturing at a presence too vast for literal anatomy but too intimate for pure abstraction either.

సర్వేంద్రియగుణాభాసం సర్వేంద్రియవివర్జితమ్  ।
అసక్తం సర్వభృచ్చైవ నిర్గుణం గుణభోక్తృ చ  ।। 15 ।।
translation_en: Although He can know all sense objects, He is senseless. He is not attached to anything, yet He is the preserver and nurturer of all. Although He is Nirguna, He is the Bhokta of the trigunas of nature.
explanation_en: Calling Brahman senseless yet capable of knowing every sense object, unattached yet the sustainer of everything, insists on holding two apparently contradictory qualities simultaneously. This isn't sloppy description — it's an attempt to point at something that ordinary either/or categories can't capture.

sanskrit_sloka:
బహిరంతశ్చ భూతానామ్ అచరం చరమేవ చ ।
సూక్ష్మత్వాత్ తదవిజ్ఞేయం దూరస్థం చాంతికే చ తత్ ।। 16 ।।
translation_en: He is present both outside and inside all material demons. He is subtle, so we cannot understand Him. Far away but also very close.
explanation_en: Being simultaneously near and far, inside and outside all beings, describes a presence that resists location entirely — not because it's absent from any particular place, but because the usual logic of position and distance simply doesn't apply to it the way it does to physical things.

sanskrit_sloka:
అవిభక్తం చ భూతేషు విభక్తమివ చ స్థితమ్ ।
భూతభర్తృ చ తద్ జ్ఞేయం గ్రసిష్ణు ప్రభవిష్ణు చ ।। 17 ।।
translation_en: He is indivisible, yet He is seen as different in all beings. Know that the Lord is the Sustainer-Sustainer, Sustainer and Creator of all bhutams (living beings).
explanation_en: Calling Brahman indivisible while appearing divided across different beings extends the same paradoxical logic into the question of multiplicity — the many beings we perceive as separate are, in this framing, not actually separate at the deepest level, however distinct they appear.
word_by_word_meaning_en: avibhaktam — indivisible; Cha — and; bhuteshu — among living beings; vibhaktam — differently divided; iva — appearing; Cha — and; sthitam — sthitudai;  bhuta-bhartru — the nurturer and protector of all living beings; Cha — and; tad — that; jneyam — knowable; grasishnu — one who makes rhythms; prabhavishnu — the creator; Cha — also.

sanskrit_sloka:
జ్యోతిషామపి తజ్జ్యోతిస్తమసః పరముచ్యతే ।
జ్ఞానం జ్ఞేయం జ్ఞానగమ్యం హృది సర్వస్య విష్ఠితమ్ ।। 18 ।।
translation_en: He is the source of light among all luminaries, and the ultimate transcendence of the darkness of ignorance. He is knowledge, He is the object of knowledge, and He is the object of knowledge. He is in the hearts of all beings.
explanation_en: Naming Brahman as both the light within all luminaries and beyond darkness, both knowledge and the object of knowledge, collapses the usual distinction between the knower, the known, and the means of knowing into a single reality, present at the very center of every being's awareness.
word_by_word_meaning_en: jyotisham — in all that is bright; api — also; tat — that; jyotih — light; tamasah — darkness; param — the transcendental; uchyate — called; jnana — knowledge; jneyam — object of knowledge; jnana-gamyam — the goal of knowledge; hrudi — in the heart; sarvasya — among all living beings; Vishthitam — will remain.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఇతి క్షేత్రం తథా జ్ఞానం జ్ఞేయం చోక్తం సమాసతః ।
మద్భక్త ఏతద్విజ్ఞాయ మద్భావాయోపపద్యతే ।। 19 ।।
translation_en: Thus I have explained to you the nature of the field, the meaning of knowledge, and the subject of knowledge. Only My devotees can truly understand this, and those who do so, they attain My divine nature.
explanation_en: Krishna's claim that only his devotees truly understand this teaching, and that understanding it leads to attaining his nature, ties this dense metaphysics back to relationship — comprehension here isn't purely intellectual achievement, it's bound up with devotion as the condition that makes real understanding possible.
word_by_word_meaning_en: iti — in this way; kshetra — the nature of the field; tatha — and; jnana — knowledge; jneyam — matter of knowledge; Cha — and; uktam — informed; samasatah — in short;  mat-bhaktah — my devotee; etat — this; vijnaya — knowing; mat-bhavah — my divine nature; Upapadyate — will get.

sanskrit_sloka:
ప్రకృతిం పురుషం చైవ విద్ధ్యనాదీ ఉభావపి ।
వికారాంశ్చ గుణాంశ్చైవ విద్ధి ప్రకృతిసంభవాన్ ।। 20 ।।
translation_en: Both Prakriti (physical nature) and Purusha (souls) are also anadiyana (sanatana). Know that all changes in the body and even the trigunas of nature are caused by material energy.
explanation_en: Declaring both Prakriti and Purusha beginningless situates this entire framework outside of time in a way that resists any origin story — neither nature nor consciousness was created at some point; both are described as having always been, with only their interactions and modifications unfolding within time.
word_by_word_meaning_en: prakriti — physical nature; purusha — living souls; Cha — and; eva — truly; viddhi — know; anadi — without beginning (aadi); ubhau — both; api — also; vicaron — changes/deformities (of the body); Cha — and; gunan — trigunas of nature; Cha — and; eva — truly; viddhi — know; prakriti — physical energy; Sambhavan — produced by.

sanskrit_sloka:
కార్యకారణకర్తృత్వే హేతుః ప్రకృతిరుచ్యతే ।
పురుషః సుఖదుఃఖానాం భోక్తృత్వే హేతురుచ్యతే ।। 21 ।।
translation_en: That physical energy is the cause of action in creation; It is said that Jivatma is responsible for experiencing pleasure and pain.
explanation_en: Assigning cause and effect within creation to Prakriti, while attributing the actual experience of pleasure and pain to the soul, divides labor cleanly: nature does the producing, the soul does the experiencing — a distinction that will matter for untangling responsibility later in the chapter.
word_by_word_meaning_en: karya — action; karana — cause; kartrutve — in generating; hetuh — reason; prakrutih — physical energy; uchyate — is said; purushah — the living soul; sukha-dukhkhanam — of the pleasures and sorrows; bhoktrtve — in experiencing; hetuh — reason; Uchyate — is called.

sanskrit_sloka:
పురుషః  ప్రకృతిస్థో హి భుంక్తే  ప్రకృతిజాన్గుణాన్ ।
కారణం గుణసంగోఽస్య  సదసద్యోనిజన్మసు ।। 22 ।।
translation_en: Whenever the Purusha (Jivatma) residing in Prakriti (physical energy) wants to enjoy the trigunas, it is Mamakarasakti for them, that Jivatma becomes the cause of high birth and low birth.
explanation_en: Explaining that the soul's entanglement with the gunas leads to births in various conditions gives a mechanism for why lives differ so much — not as arbitrary fate, but as a direct consequence of which qualities of nature a soul has become identified with and drawn toward.
word_by_word_meaning_en: purushah — the living soul; prakriti-sthah — situated in nature; hi — truly; bhunkte — indulge; prakriti-jan — born of physical energy (prakriti); gunan — the trigunas; cause — cause; guna-sangah — union with the qualities (mamakarasakti); asya — of that; sat-asat-yoni — in the noble-vile-womb; Janmasu — to be born.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఉపద్రష్టానుమంతా చ భర్తా భోక్తా మహేశ్వరః ।
పరమాత్మేతి చాప్యుక్తో దేహేఽస్మిన్ పురుషః పరః ।। 23 ।।
translation_en: The Supreme Lord also resides in the body itself. He is said to be the All-Witness, the All-Appointer, the Sustainer, the Eternal Sustainer, the Supreme Authority and the Supreme Soul.
explanation_en: Describing the Supreme Lord as witness, permitter, sustainer, and supreme soul, dwelling within the very same body as the individual self, adds a third presence to the picture beyond just the field and its ordinary knower — an overseeing awareness present within, but distinct from, personal experience.
word_by_word_meaning_en: upadrashta — witness; anumantha — the giver of the elephant; Cha — and; bhartra — husband (supporter); bhokta — the transcendental bhokta; maha-isvarah — the supreme controller/authority; parama-atma — the supreme soul; iti — that; cha api — even more; uktah — is said; dehe — in the body; asmin — this; purushah-parah — the Supreme Lord.

sanskrit_sloka:
య ఏవం వేత్తి పురుషం ప్రకృతిం చ గుణైః సహ ।
సర్వథా వర్తమానోఽపి న స భూయోఽభిజాయతే ।। 24 ।।
translation_en: Those who understand the reality of the trinity of Paramatma, Jivatma, material nature and prakriti, will never be born here again. They will be liberated regardless of their current condition.
explanation_en: The promise that understanding this three-part reality — Supreme Self, individual self, and material nature — prevents future rebirth regardless of one's current condition offers real hope independent of circumstance. It isn't about starting from purity; it's about eventually arriving at correct understanding.
word_by_word_meaning_en: yah — whoever; evam — thus; vetti — deciphered; purusha — male; prakriti — physical nature; Cha — and; gunaih — the three modes of nature; co — with; sarvatha — of all kinds; vartamanah — established; api — even so; na — not; sah — they; bhuyah — again; abhijayate — to be born.

sanskrit_sloka:
ధ్యానేనాత్మని పశ్యంతి కేచిదాత్మానమాత్మనా ।
అన్యే సాంఖ్యేన యోగేన కర్మయోగేన చాపరే ।। 25 ।।
translation_en: Some try to see the divine in their heart through meditation; And others seek to attain this through the acquisition of knowledge, and still others strive to attain this knowledge through the path of karma.
explanation_en: Naming three different routes to the same realization — meditation, philosophical knowledge, and disciplined action — refuses to elevate one method as the only valid path. Different temperaments, Krishna suggests, can each find their own workable route to the same destination.

sanskrit_sloka:
అన్యే త్వేవమజానంతః శ్రుత్వాన్యేభ్య ఉపాసతే ।
తేఽపి చాతితరంత్యేవ మృత్యుం శ్రుతిపరాయణాః ।। 26 ।।
translation_en: And some who are not aware of these spiritual paths, hear about them from others and start worshiping the Supreme Lord.  By listening to the Mahatmas with devotion like this, they too can gradually cross this ocean of birth and death.
explanation_en: Including even those who simply hear about this from others and begin worshipping without deep personal study is a notably generous inclusion — it suggests sincere trust in a teacher or tradition, absent independent mastery, can still eventually carry a person across the same difficult crossing.
word_by_word_meaning_en: anye — others; tu — yet; evam — thus; ajanantah — those who do not know (about spiritual paths); srutva — by hearing; anyebhya — from others; upasate — begins to worship; te — they; api — also; Cha — and; atitaranti — passes over;  eva — also; mrityum — death; sruti parayanah — hearing with devotion (by the great souls).

sanskrit_sloka:
యావత్సంజాయతే కించిత్ సత్త్వం స్థావరజంగమమ్ ।
క్షేత్రక్షేత్రజ్ఞసంయోగాత్ తద్విద్ధి భరతర్షభ ।। 27 ।।
translation_en: O best of the Bharatas, know that you are all these living creatures, this field and the union of the Kshetrajna.
explanation_en: Krishna's direct address — telling Arjuna he himself is this union of field and knower — personalizes what had become fairly abstract discussion. This isn't just theory about bodies and souls in general; it's a statement about what Arjuna specifically is, right now, in this very conversation.
word_by_word_meaning_en: yavat — all; sanjayate — manifested; kinchit — whatever; sattva — creature; புத்திய் — bases (immovable); jangamam — moving;  kshetra — the field; Kshetrajna — Kshetrajna (one who knows the field); sanyogat — due to conjunction; tat — that; viddhi — know; Bharata-rishabha — The best of the Bharata clan.

sanskrit_sloka:
సమం సర్వేషు భూతేషు తిష్ఠంతం పరమేశ్వరమ్ ।
వినశ్యత్స్వవినశ్యంతం యః పశ్యతి స పశ్యతి ।। 28 ।।
translation_en: He who sees the Supreme Being in all living beings with their souls, and who sees both as impermanent in this transitory body, is truly seen.
explanation_en: Seeing the Supreme Being equally present within every living being, while recognizing the perishable nature of the body itself, is named here as genuine sight — implying that most ordinary perception, focused only on the temporary form, isn't really seeing clearly at all.
word_by_word_meaning_en: samam — equally; sarveshu — all; bhuteshu — among the living beings; Tishthantam — keep following;  parama-esvaram — the Supreme Being; vinashyatsu — among perishables; avinasyantam — being imperishable; yah — whoever; pasyati — see; sah — they; Pasyati — as seen.

sanskrit_sloka:
సమం పశ్యన్ హి సర్వత్ర సమవస్థితమీశ్వరమ్ ।
న హినస్త్యాత్మనాత్మానం తతో యాతి పరాం గతిమ్ ।। 29 ।।
translation_en: Those who see that Lord, who is equal to all beings, the Supreme Soul, do not degrade themselves with their minds. Thus, they reach the Supreme Word.
explanation_en: Not degrading oneself through the mind, once this equal vision of the Supreme Soul in all beings is achieved, suggests that self-harm and self-diminishment are, at root, failures of perception — seeing correctly is described as protective, almost automatically preventing certain kinds of inner damage.
word_by_word_meaning_en: samam — equally; pashyan — visited; hi — truly; sarvatra — everywhere; samavasthitam — evenly situated; Isvaram — the Supreme Lord; na — does not; hinasti — to degrade; atmana — by the mind; atmanam — the soul; tatah — so that; yati — reaches; param — the Supreme; Path — destination.

sanskrit_sloka:
ప్రకృత్యైవ చ కర్మాణి క్రియమాణాని సర్వశః ।
యః పశ్యతి తథాత్మానమ్ అకర్తారం స పశ్యతి ।। 30 ।।
translation_en: It is the physical nature that does all the work (of the body) and the Jivatma actually does nothing - as one who understands has truly seen.
explanation_en: Recognizing that material nature performs all actions, while the self does nothing, offers real relief from a common source of anxiety: the exhausting sense of being solely responsible for every outcome. Seeing this correctly, Krishna suggests, is what genuine insight actually looks like.
word_by_word_meaning_en: prakritya — by the nature of nature; eva — truly; Cha — and; karmani — karmas; kriyamanani — to be done; sarvasah — all;  yah — whoever; pasyati — not seen; tatha — also; atmanam — the living soul; akartaram — akarta (does nothing); sa — they; Pasyati — as seen.

sanskrit_sloka:
యదా భూతపృథగ్భావమ్ ఏకస్థమనుపశ్యతి ।
తత ఏవ చ విస్తారం బ్రహ్మ సంపద్యతే తదా ।। 31 ।।
translation_en: When they see that all beings with different qualities are situated in the same Prakriti, and understand that they are all emanated from the same, they attain knowledge of Brahman.
explanation_en: Seeing the diversity of beings as situated within a single underlying nature, all emanating from the same source despite their apparent differences, extends the equal vision from verse 28 into the material world itself — variety and unity aren't opposed here, they coexist.

sanskrit_sloka:
అనాదిత్వాన్నిర్గుణత్వాత్ పరమాత్మాయమవ్యయః ।
శరీరస్థోఽపి కౌంతేయ న కరోతి న లిప్యతే ।। 32 ।।
translation_en: O son of Kunti, the Supreme Personality of Godhead is imperishable, eternal, without any physical attributes. Although present in the body, He does nothing, and is not at all tainted by material energy.
explanation_en: Describing the Supreme as imperishable, without qualities, untouched despite being present in the body, uses the same paradox pattern from earlier in the chapter — presence without contamination, involvement without being altered by what one is involved with.

sanskrit_sloka:
యథా సర్వగతం సౌక్ష్మ్యాత్ ఆకాశం నోపలిప్యతే ।
సర్వత్రావస్థితో దేహే తథాత్మా నోపలిప్యతే ।। 33 ।।
translation_en: Akasa (empty space) contains everything within itself, but being subtle, is not tainted by what it contains. Similarly, although all its consciousness is pervaded in the body, the soul is not affected by the qualities of the body.
explanation_en: The comparison to space — present everywhere yet unstained by anything it contains — gives this abstract claim a concrete, almost physical intuition to hold onto: just as air fills a room without picking up the room's dust, the soul can pervade the body without absorbing its limitations.

sanskrit_sloka:
యథా ప్రకాశయత్యేకః  కృత్స్నం లోకమిమం రవిః ।
క్షేత్రం క్షేత్రీ తథా కృత్స్నం ప్రకాశయతి  భారత  ।। 34 ।।
translation_en: Just as one sun illuminates the entire solar system, so one soul illuminates the entire body (consciousness).
explanation_en: The single-sun image, illuminating an entire solar system from one source, offers the chapter's clearest visual for how one awareness can pervade an entire body — not scattered or diluted across it, but wholly present, the way light doesn't divide itself among the things it touches.

sanskrit_sloka:
క్షేత్రక్షేత్రజ్ఞయోరేవమ్ అంతరం జ్ఞానచక్షుషా ।
భూతప్రకృతిమోక్షం చ యే విదుర్యాంతి తే పరమ్ ।। 35 ।।
translation_en: Those who observe the distinction of this ksetra and the ksetrajna with knowledge-eyes, and who know the method of liberation from material nature, attain the Supreme Padma.
explanation_en: The chapter's closing promise — that seeing the distinction between the field and its knower with real clarity leads to liberation from material entanglement — ties the whole discussion back to its opening question, confirming that this entire technical unpacking was never abstract for its own sake, but aimed squarely at freedom.

sanskrit_sloka:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ ।
పరం భూయః  ప్రవక్ష్యామి  జ్ఞానానాం జ్ఞానముత్తమమ్ ।
యద్ జ్ఞాత్వా మునయః  సర్వే  పరాం సిద్ధిమితో గతాః  ।। 1 ।।
translation_en: Sri Bhagavan said: I will once again explain to you this supreme education, the best of all knowledge; Knowing this, all the great saints attained the highest perfection.
explanation_en: Krishna's promise to explain this 'once again,' calling it the best of all knowledge, signals that what follows isn't a minor addendum — the claim that great sages reached the highest perfection through exactly this teaching sets real expectations before a single guna has been named.
word_by_word_meaning_en: Sri- bhagavan-uvacha — the Lord spoke thus; param — the Supreme; bhuyah — again; pravakshyami — I explain; jnanam — of all knowledge; jnanam-uttamam — supreme knowledge; yat  — whatever; jnatva — knowing pidapa; munayah — the ancestors; Survey — All; param — the supreme; siddhim — perfection (siddhi); itah — by this; gatah  — obtained.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఇదం జ్ఞానముపాశ్రిత్య మమ సాధర్మ్యమాగతాః ।
సర్గేఽపి నోపజాయంతే ప్రలయే న వ్యథంతి చ ।। 2 ।।
translation_en: Those who take refuge in this knowledge will reach me. They are neither reborn at the time of creation nor destroyed at the time of Pralaya.
explanation_en: Freedom from being reborn at creation or destroyed at dissolution describes a kind of permanence beyond even cosmic cycles — most spiritual promises operate within the frame of one lifetime; this one operates on a scale where entire universes rise and fall while the liberated remain untouched.
word_by_word_meaning_en: This — this; jnanam — knowledge; upashritya — resorting to; mama — of me; saadharmyam — such nature;  agatah — obtained pidapa;  sarge — at the time of creation; api — also; na upajayante — not born; pralaye — at the time of pralaya; na-vyathanti — does not suffer; Cha — and.

sanskrit_sloka: ['మమ యోనిర్మహద్బ్రహ్మ తస్మిన్గర్భం దధామ్యహమ్ ।\nసంభవః సర్వభూతానాం తతో భవతి భారత ।। 3 ।।', 'సర్వయోనిషు కౌంతేయ మూర్తయః సంభవంతి యాః ।\nతాసాం బ్రహ్మ మహద్యోనిః అహం బీజప్రదః పితా ।। 4 ।।']
translation_en: Its all physical nature, womb. Into it I introduce different souls, thus all living beings are born. O son of Kunti, this physical nature is the womb and I am the seed-giving father of all the living beings born.
explanation_en: The image of physical nature as a womb, with Krishna as the seed-giving source of all life born into it, gives creation a strikingly intimate, almost biological framing rather than a mechanical or abstract one — origin is described in terms of parentage, not just causation.

translation_en: Its all physical nature, womb. Into it I introduce different souls, thus all living beings are born. O son of Kunti, this physical nature is the womb and I am the seed-giving father of all the living beings born.
explanation_en: Repeating the womb-and-seed image reinforces how central this metaphor is to what follows — before breaking beings down by which guna dominates them, Krishna first wants Arjuna to hold onto the basic picture of where every living thing, regardless of its qualities, actually comes from.
