sanskrit_sloka:
అసక్తబుద్ధిః సర్వత్ర జితాత్మా విగతస్పృహః ।
నైష్కర్మ్యసిద్ధిం పరమాం సన్న్యాసేనాధిగచ్ఛతి ।। 49 ।।
translation_en: Whose intellect is dispassionate throughout, who conquers the mind and renounces desires through the practice of asceticism, attains the supreme Naishkarmya Siddhi.
explanation_en: Describing the culmination of this disciplined detachment — dispassionate intellect, conquered mind, released desire — as reaching the state of 'naishkarmya siddhi,' perfection beyond the need for further action, gives a name to the endpoint the whole chapter's analysis has been building toward.
word_by_word_meaning_en: asakta-buddhih — whose mind is disinterested; sarvatra — throughout; jita-atma — subjugated the mind; vigata-sakshamah — without desires; naishkarmya-siddhim — the karma-free state; param — the supreme; sannyasena — by the practice of asceticism;  Adhigacchhati — obtains.

sanskrit_sloka:
సిద్ధిం ప్రాప్తో యథా బ్రహ్మ తథాప్నోతి నిబోధ మే ।
సమాసేనైవ కౌంతేయ నిష్ఠా జ్ఞానస్య యా పరా ।। 50 ।।
translation_en: O Arjuna, how one who has attained perfect siddhi (in karmic asceticism) can attain Brahman also by being established in transcendental spiritual knowledge - hear me in brief.
explanation_en: Promising a brief explanation of how this perfected state connects to full realization of Brahman signals the chapter is entering its final movement — from analysis and classification into the most direct, condensed instruction Krishna is willing to offer.

sanskrit_sloka:
['బుద్ధ్యా విశుద్దయా యుక్తో ధృత్యాత్మానం నియమ్య చ ।
శబ్దాదీన్ విషయాన్ త్యక్త్వా రాగద్వేషౌ వ్యుదస్య చ ।। 51 ।।', 'వివిక్తసేవీ లఘ్వాశీ యతవాక్కాయమానసః ।
ధ్యానయోగపరో నిత్యం వైరాగ్యం సముపాశ్రితః ।। 52 ।।', 'అహంకారం బలం దర్పం కామ క్రోధం పరిగ్రహమ్ ।
విముచ్య నిర్మమః శాంతో బ్రహ్మభూయాయ కల్పతే ।। 53 ।।']
translation_en: When a person - has a pure intellect, and has well restrained the senses, renounces sound and other sense objects, and is free from hatred of raga, then he is fit to attain Brahman. Such a person likes solitude, eats in moderation, controls body language, engages in constant meditation and practices dispassion. A person who is free from ego, violence, avarice, desires, selfishness, selfishness - is peaceful and deserves to attain the state of oneness with the Supreme Being. (ie, knowing the Supreme Truth in the form of Brahman).
explanation_en: The extended description of the qualified aspirant — pure intellect, disciplined senses, released from sound and sensory craving, free from attachment and aversion — reads as a final composite portrait, drawing together threads from across the entire text into one figure.

(ie, knowing the Supreme Truth in the form of Brahman).
explanation_en: Continuing the portrait with a preference for solitude, moderate eating, controlled speech and body, constant meditation, and cultivated detachment fills in the practical, daily texture of this figure's life — not abstract virtue alone, but specific, livable habits.

sanskrit_sloka:
బ్రహ్మభూతః ప్రసన్నాత్మా న శోచతి న కాంక్షతి ।
సమః సర్వేషు భూతేషు మద్భక్తిం లభతే పరామ్ ।। 54 ।।
translation_en: A person who is at one with Parabrahman is mentally calm, does not grieve for anything, does not desire for anything. Being equanimous towards all beings, such a yogi will receive my parabhakti.
explanation_en: Someone established in Brahman is described as mentally serene, free from grief and craving, equally disposed toward all beings — and this state, Krishna says, is precisely what qualifies a person to receive his supreme devotion, para-bhakti, connecting realization directly to relationship.
word_by_word_meaning_en: brahma-bhutah — who is situated in the Brahman sense; prasanna-atma — with mental calmness; na shochati — do not mourn; na kankshati — does not desire; samah — with an equal spirit; sarveshu — to all; bhuteshu — beings (demons);  mat-bhaktim — devotion to Me; labhate — gets; param — the supreme.

sanskrit_sloka:
భక్త్యా మామభిజానాతి యావాన్యశ్చాస్మి తత్త్వతః ।
తతో మాం తత్త్వతో జ్ఞాత్వా విశతే తదనంతరమ్ ।। 55 ।।
translation_en: Only through loving devotion to Me can I know who (how much) I really am. Knowing Me, Pidapa, My devotee is absorbed in My absolute consciousness.
explanation_en: The claim that only through loving devotion can Krishna truly be known, and that knowing him this way leads to complete absorption in him, positions bhakti not as an alternative to the philosophical realization just described but as its actual gateway and completion.
word_by_word_meaning_en: bhaktya — by loving devotion; mam — me; abhijanati — knows; yavan — how much; yah cha asmi — as I am; tattvatah — actually; tatah — then; mam — me; tattvatah — in the true form; jnatva — knowing; visate — enters; After that — after that.

sanskrit_sloka:
సర్వకర్మాణ్యపి సదా కుర్వాణో మద్వ్యపాశ్రయః ।
మత్ప్రసాదాదవాప్నోతి శాశ్వతం పదమవ్యయమ్ ।। 56 ।।
translation_en: My devotees take full refuge in Me even though they are doing all the activities. By my grace they will attain eternal and impermanent abode.
explanation_en: Devotees who take full refuge in Krishna while still engaged in all their ordinary activities are promised, by his grace, an eternal and unchanging abode — action and devotion aren't shown as competing again here; full engagement in life coexists with complete inner refuge.
word_by_word_meaning_en: sarva — all; karmani — works; api — also; sada — always; kurvanah — performing; mat-vyapashrayah — taking complete refuge in Me; mat prasadat — by my grace; avapnoti — get; स्वात्मा — eternal; padam — abode; avyam — ephemeral.

sanskrit_sloka:
చేతసా సర్వకర్మాణి మయి సన్న్యస్య మత్పరః ।
బుద్ధియోగముపాశ్రిత్య మచ్చిత్తః సతతం భవ ।। 57 ।।
translation_en: Make me your supreme goal and offer your every karma to me. Take refuge in Buddhi Yoga and make your will always ascend to me.
explanation_en: The instruction to make Krishna the supreme goal, offering every action to him, taking refuge in disciplined understanding with the will constantly directed toward him, condenses the whole practical teaching of the text into a single compact formula near its close.
word_by_word_meaning_en: chetasa — intahkarana do; sarva-karmani — of all karmas; mai — to me; sannyasya — surrendering; matparah — with me as the supreme goal; buddhi-yoga — uniting the mind with God; upashritya — resorting to; mat-chittah — make chitta ascendant to me; satatam — always; bhava — stay.

sanskrit_sloka:
మచ్చిత్తః సర్వదుర్గాణి మత్ప్రసాదాత్ తరిష్యసి ।
అథ చేత్ త్వమహంకారాత్ న శ్రోష్యసి వినంక్ష్యసి ।। 58 ।।
translation_en: If you always remember Me, by My grace you can overcome all obstacles and difficulties. But if, through pride, you do not listen to my advice, you will perish.
explanation_en: The promise that remembering Krishna will carry Arjuna past every obstacle, paired with the warning that ignoring this counsel out of pride leads to ruin, states the stakes with unusual directness — not gentle suggestion here, but a clear consequence attached to the choice.
word_by_word_meaning_en: mat-cittah — always remembering Me; sarva — all; durgani — hindrances; mat-prasadat — by my grace; tarishyasi — may you overcome; atha — but; cet — if; tvam — you; ahamkarat — by arrogance; na sroshyasi — if not heard ; Vinamkshyasi — you will be destroyed.

sanskrit_sloka:
యదహంకారమాశ్రిత్య న యోత్స్య ఇతి మన్యసే ।
మిథ్యైష వ్యవసాయస్తే ప్రకృతిస్త్వాం నియోక్ష్యతి ।। 59 ।।
translation_en: If you are motivated by pride and think, "I will not fight," then your decision will be wasted anyway. Because it is your own (Kshatriya) physical nature that impels you to fight.
explanation_en: Krishna's blunt prediction that Arjuna's resolve not to fight will prove futile, because his own warrior nature will compel him regardless, cuts through any illusion that willpower alone can override deeply rooted disposition — refusal here isn't even presented as a real option.

sanskrit_sloka:
స్వభావజేన కౌంతేయ నిబద్ధః స్వేన కర్మణా ।
కర్తుం నేచ్ఛసి యన్మోహాత్ కరిష్యస్యవశోఽపి తత్ ।। 60 ।।
translation_en: O Arjuna, whatever action you say you will not do due to lust, you will be prompted to do it by the impulse born of your natural nature.
explanation_en: Extending this point — that whatever Arjuna refuses to do out of delusion, his own nature will eventually drive him to do anyway — generalizes beyond this one battlefield decision into a broader claim about the power of inherent disposition over surface-level resistance.
word_by_word_meaning_en: svabhava-jena — born of natural nature; Kaunteya — Arjuna, son of the goddess Kunti; nibadah — bound; svena — thine own; karmana — karmas; kartum — to do; na icchasi — if you do not want; yat — whatever; mohat — by passion; karishyasi — you do; avasah — subdued; api — even so; tat — that.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఈశ్వరః సర్వభూతానాం హృద్దేశేఽర్జున తిష్ఠతి ।
భ్రామయన్ సర్వభూతాని యంత్రారూఢాని మాయయా ।। 61 ।।
translation_en: Ishvara resides in the heart of all beings, O Arjuna. He directs the course of the living souls who ascend the Yantra made of material energy, according to their respective karmas.
explanation_en: Describing the divine as seated in the heart of every being, directing all creatures through the mechanism of material nature according to their karma, gives a cosmic frame to the personal prediction just made — Arjuna's individual struggle is placed within a much larger governing order.

sanskrit_sloka:
తమేవ శరణం గచ్ఛ సర్వభావేన భారత ।
తత్ప్రసాదాత్పరాం శాంతిం స్థానం ప్రాప్స్యసి శాశ్వతమ్ ।। 62 ।।
translation_en: Surrender completely to Him alone, O Bharata.  By His grace, you will attain supreme peace and eternal abode.
explanation_en: The instruction to take complete refuge in this indwelling divine presence, promised to lead to supreme peace and an eternal abode by grace, offers the resolution to everything just described — not fighting one's nature, but surrendering the outcome entirely to what already directs it.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఇతి తే జ్ఞానమాఖ్యాతం గుహ్యాద్గుహ్యతరం మయా ।
విమృశ్యైతదశేషేణ యథేచ్ఛసి తథా కురు ।। 63 ।।
translation_en: Thus I have revealed to you the most secret knowledge of all secrets. Think deeply about it, and do as you like.
explanation_en: Calling this the most confidential knowledge of all, then explicitly leaving the final decision to Arjuna — 'do as you like' — is a remarkable moment of restraint after seventeen-plus chapters of instruction. Krishna teaches everything, then steps back and hands the choice over completely.
word_by_word_meaning_en: iti — in this way; te — to you; jnana — knowledge; akhyatam — described; guhyat — than secret knowledge; guhya-taram — yet mysterious knowledge; maya — by me; vimrisya — thinking well; etat — on that; aseshena — completely; yatha — if a; ichchasi — if desired; tatha — in that way; kuru — do.

sanskrit_sloka:
సర్వగుహ్యతమం భూయః శృణు మే పరమం వచః ।
ఇష్టోఽసి మే ధృఢమితి తతో వక్ష్యామి తే హితమ్ ।। 64 ।।
translation_en: Hear once again My supreme instruction, which is the most secret of all knowledge. I am telling you this for your sake, because you are very dear to me.
explanation_en: Offering to repeat the supreme instruction 'once again,' specifically because Arjuna is dear to him, reintroduces personal affection as the final motive for teaching — not obligation or cosmic necessity, but simple care for someone Krishna considers a beloved friend.
word_by_word_meaning_en: sarva-guhya-tama — more mysterious than all; bhuyah — again; srinu — hear; May — by me; param — supreme; vacah — instruction; ishtah-asi — You are beloved; may — to me; dhridham — very;  iti — in this way; tatah — because; vaksyami — I utter; te — of you; Hitam — seeking hitam (well-being).

sanskrit_sloka:
మన్మనా భవ మద్భక్తో మద్యాజీ మాం నమస్కురు ।
మామేవైష్యసి సత్యం తే ప్రతిజానే ప్రియోఽసి మే ।। 65 ।।
translation_en: Always remember Me, be devoted to Me, worship Me and bow to Me. By doing this you will surely reach me. This is my promise to you, because you are very dear to me.
explanation_en: The instruction to constantly remember, worship, and bow to Krishna, with the promise that doing so guarantees reaching him, is about as direct and unconditional as any promise in the text — no qualifications attached, just a plain assurance backed by Krishna's own word.
word_by_word_meaning_en: mat-mana — remembering me; bhava — be; mat-bhaktah — as my devotee; mat-yaji — worship Me; mam — to me; namaskuru — pay obeisance; Mom — me; eva — truly; aeshyasi — reaching; satyam — truthfully; te — to you; pratijane — I promise; priyah — beloved; asi — you; May — to me.

sanskrit_sloka:
సర్వధర్మాన్ పరిత్యజ్య మామేకం శరణం వ్రజ ।
అహం త్వాం సర్వపాపేభ్యో మోక్షయిష్యామి మా శుచః ।। 66 ।।
translation_en: Abandon all kinds of dharmas and surrender to Me alone. I will absolve you of all sins, fear not.
explanation_en: The most famous line in the entire Gita — abandon all dharmas and take refuge in Krishna alone, and he will free Arjuna from all sin — arrives as the culmination of everything before it. After chapters spent carefully defending duty, the final instruction moves past duty entirely into total surrender.
word_by_word_meaning_en: sarva-dharmaan — all kinds of dharmas; parityajya — abandoning; Mom — in me; ekam — only; sharanam — refuge; vraja — get; Aham — I; tvam — you; sarva — all; papebhyah — from sinful reactions; mokshaishyami — liberating; Ma Shuchah — do not be afraid.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఇదం తే నాతపస్కాయ నాభక్తాయ కదాచన ।
న చాశుశ్రూషవే వాచ్యం న చ మాం యోఽభ్యసూయతి ।। 67 ।।
translation_en: This Upadesha should never be given to a non-ascetic, a non-pious person. (Spiritual matters) Do not say this even to those who are averse to hearing, and especially to those who are envious of me.
explanation_en: The instruction never to share this teaching with those lacking discipline or devotion, or with those who resist hearing it or resent Krishna, protects the teaching's integrity — not everything valuable, Krishna suggests, is helpful to everyone regardless of their readiness to receive it.
word_by_word_meaning_en: This — this; te — by you; na — should not; athapaskaya — for those who are not ascetics; na — should not; abhaktaya — for non-devotees; kadachana — never; na — should not; cha — become; asushrushave — for those who are interested in hearing (spiritual matters); vachyam — telling; na — should never; Cha — and; mam — towards me; yah — whoever; Abhyasuyati — For those who are envious/jealous.

sanskrit_sloka:
య ఇదం పరమం గుహ్యం మద్భక్తేష్వభిధాస్యతి ।
భక్తిం మయి పరాం కృత్వా మామేవైష్యత్యసంశయః ।। 68 ।।
translation_en: Whoever inculcates this supremely secret knowledge among My devotees, they have performed supreme loving service. They will undoubtedly reach me.
explanation_en: Whoever shares this most confidential knowledge among Krishna's devotees is said to have performed the highest loving service, guaranteed to reach him — transmission of the teaching itself becomes an act of devotion equal to, or greater than, personal practice alone.
word_by_word_meaning_en: yah — whoever; Itam — of this; param — supreme; guhyam — secret knowledge; madbhakteshu — among my devotees; abhidhasyati — instructs;  bhaktim — supreme love; mai — to me; param — transcendental; kritva — doing; Mom — me; eva — truly; eshyati — reaches; asamsayah — without doubt.

sanskrit_sloka:
న చ తస్మాన్మనుష్యేషు కశ్చిన్మే ప్రియకృత్తమః ।
భవితా న చ మే తస్మాదన్యః ప్రియతరో భువి ।। 69 ।।
translation_en: No one has done me more loving service than they; There will be no one on this earth dearer to me than they.
explanation_en: The claim that no one performs greater service, and no one will be dearer to Krishna, elevates teaching and sharing this knowledge to the very top of devotional acts — a striking emphasis on generosity of understanding as the highest expression of love.
word_by_word_meaning_en: na — not; Cha — and; tasmat — beyond them; manushyeshu — among men; kaschit — anyone; may — to me; priya-krit-tamah — more beloved; bhavita — not going to be; na — not; Cha — and; may — to me; tasmat — than them; anyah — someone else; priya-tarah — dear ones; bhuvi — on this earth.

sanskrit_sloka:
అధ్యేష్యతే చ య ఇమం ధర్మ్యం సంవాదమావయోః ।
జ్ఞానయజ్ఞేన తేనాహమిష్టః స్యామితి మే మతిః ।। 70 ।।
translation_en: Those who recite this holy dialogue between us, worship Me with the sacrifice of knowledge (with their intellects); That is my opinion.
explanation_en: Those who study this dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna are said to worship through the sacrifice of knowledge — even engagement with the text itself, independent of direct devotional practice, is counted as a genuine form of worship in its own right.
word_by_word_meaning_en: adhyeshyate — chanting; Cha — and; yah — whoever; imam — this; dharmyam — pious; samvadam — conversation; avayoh — of us; jnana — knowledge; yajnena thena — by jnana yajna; Aham — I; ishtah — to be worshipped; Sam — will be; iti — this; May — of me; matih — opinion.

sanskrit_sloka:
శ్రద్ధావాననసూయశ్చ శృణుయాదపి యో నరః ।
సోఽపి ముక్తః శుభాల్లోకాన్ ప్ర్రాప్నుయాత్ పుణ్యకర్మణామ్ ।। 71 ।।
translation_en: Even those who merely hear this knowledge, with earnest faith and without envy, are freed from sins and reach the holy worlds where the pious souls reside.
explanation_en: Even those who merely hear this teaching with sincere faith and without envy are said to be freed from sin and to reach the worlds of the righteous — the bar for benefit is set remarkably low, open even to someone encountering the teaching for the very first time.
word_by_word_meaning_en: shraddha-van — possessing diligence/faith; anasuyah — without envy; Cha — and; srinuyat — if heard; api — certainly; yah — whoever; narah — person; sah — that person; api — also; muktah — liberated; shubhan — auspicious; lokan — the worlds; prapnuyat — gets; punya-karmanam — of the pious souls.

sanskrit_sloka:
కచ్చిదేతఛ్చ్రుతం పార్థ త్వయైకాగ్రేణ చేతసా ।
కచ్చిదజ్ఞానసమ్మోహః ప్రణష్టస్తే ధనంజయ ।। 72 ।।
translation_en: O Arjuna, did you listen attentively to what I said? Are your ignorance and delusion eradicated?
explanation_en: Krishna's closing question — did you listen carefully, has your confusion been dispelled — turns the conversation directly back toward Arjuna one final time, checking not whether the teaching was complete, but whether it actually landed.
word_by_word_meaning_en: Kachit — happened? etat — this; srutam — hearing; Partha — Arjuna, son of Pritha; tvaya — by you; eka-agrena-chetasa — with single-mindedness; Kachit — is it? ajna — ignorance; sammohah — delusion/delusion; pranashtah — to be eradicated; te — of you; Dhananjayah — Arjuna, conqueror of wealth.

sanskrit_sloka:
అర్జున ఉవాచ ।
నష్టో మోహః స్మృతిర్లబ్ధా త్వత్ప్రసాదాన్మయాచ్యుత ।
స్థితోఽస్మి గతసందేహః కరిష్యే వచనం తవ ।। 73 ।।
translation_en: Arjuna said: O Achyuta (blameless one), by your grace my delusion is eradicated, and I am established in knowledge. I have no doubts now, and will do according to your instructions.
explanation_en: Arjuna's answer — his delusion destroyed, his memory restored, ready to act according to Krishna's word, doubt-free — provides genuine closure to the arc that opened in chapter 1, transforming his initial collapse into settled clarity and resolve.
word_by_word_meaning_en: Arjuna Uvacha — Arjuna spoke; rastah — eradicated; moha — delusion; smritih — memory; labda — got back; tvat-prasadat — by Your grace;  maya — by me; Achyuta — Sri Krishna, the faultless one; sthitah — standing still; asmi — I; gata-sandehah — without doubts; karishye — I will; Text — Admonitions; tava — of you.

sanskrit_sloka:
సంజయ ఉవాచ ।
ఇత్యహం వాసుదేవస్య పార్థస్య చ మహాత్మనః ।
సంవాదమిమమశ్రౌషమ్ అద్భుతం రోమహర్షణమ్ ।। 74 ।।
translation_en: Sanjay said: Thus, I, heard the conversation between Lord Krishna, son of Vasudeva, and Arjuna, son of Mahatma, Pritha. It's so amazing it makes my hair stand on end.
explanation_en: Sanjaya's description of his hair standing on end while recounting this conversation shifts the perspective outward — the narrator, previously an invisible reporter, now registers his own visceral response to what he's just relayed, underlining how extraordinary the exchange has been.
word_by_word_meaning_en: Sanjaya Uwacha — Sanjayadu Palikenu; iti — in this way; Aham — I; vasudevasya — of Sri Krishna; parthasya — Arjuna; Cha — and; maha-atmanah — the great soul; samvadam — dialogue; imam — this; Asrausham — heard Pidapa; awesome — amazing; Roma-harshanam — makes the hair (hair) stand out.

sanskrit_sloka:
వ్యాసప్రసాదాఛ్చ్రుతవాన్ ఏతద్గుహ్యమహం పరమ్ ।
యోగం యోగేశ్వరాత్ కృష్ణాత్ సాక్షాత్ కథయతః స్వయమ్ ।। 75 ।।
translation_en: By the grace of Vedavyasa, I learned this supreme secret of yoga from Lord Krishna himself.
explanation_en: Crediting Vyasa's grace for his ability to hear this teaching directly from Krishna situates Sanjaya's own privileged access within a larger lineage of transmission — even the narrator's position as witness is presented as a gift rather than an accident.
word_by_word_meaning_en: vyasa-prasadat — by the grace of Vedic Vyasa; srutavan — heard; etat — this; guhyam — secret; Aham — I; param — supreme; yoga — yoga; yoga-esvarat — from Yogeshvara; krishnat — from Sri Krishna; sakshat — directly; kathayatah — uttered; Swayam — Himself by Himself.

sanskrit_sloka:
రాజన్ సంస్మృత్య సంస్మృత్య సంవాదమిమమద్భుతమ్ ।
కేశవార్జునయోః పుణ్యం హృష్యామి చ ముహుర్ముహుః ।। 76 ।।
translation_en: I am rejoicing over and over again recalling this magnificent conversation between the Supreme Lord Sri Krishna and Arjuna.
explanation_en: Sanjaya's admission that he keeps rejoicing again and again simply from remembering this conversation captures something about teachings of this magnitude — their impact doesn't diminish with recollection, but seems to renew itself each time they're brought back to mind.
word_by_word_meaning_en: Rajan — king; samsmrtya samsmrtya — remembering again and again; samvadam — conversation; imam — this; amadbhutam — excellent; kesava-arjunayoh — between Sri Krishna Paramatma and Arjuna; punyam — pious; hrishyami — enjoying; Cha — and; Muhuh -muhuh — repeatedly (continually).

sanskrit_sloka:
తచ్చ సంస్మృత్య సంస్మృత్య రూపమత్యద్భుతం హరేః ।
విస్మయో మే మహాన్ రాజన్ హృష్యామి చ పునఃపునః ।। 77 ।।
translation_en: And, remembering the wonderful and astonishing cosmic form of Sri Krishna, I am amazed and thrilled with great joy again and again.
explanation_en: Recalling Krishna's astonishing cosmic form specifically alongside the conversation itself shows how thoroughly the vision from chapter 11 remains bound up with everything that followed it — Sanjaya's wonder circles back to that singular revelation even at the very end.
word_by_word_meaning_en: tat — that; Cha — and; samsmrtya samsmrtya — remembering again and again; rupam — cosmic form; ati-abhutam — excellent; hareh — of Sri Krishna; vismayah — with awe; May — of me; mahan — great; rajan — the king; hrishyami — exulting in joy; Cha — and; Again and again — again and again.

sanskrit_sloka:
యత్ర యోగేశ్వరః కృష్ణో యత్ర పార్థో ధనుర్ధరః ।
తత్ర శ్రీర్విజయో భూతిః ధ్రువా నీతిర్మతిర్మమ ।। 78 ।।
translation_en: It is my firm opinion that wherever Sri Krishna, the Yogeshwar, and Arjuna, the supreme archer, are there, there is all wealth, all victory, all-plenty and righteousness.
explanation_en: The Gita's final verse — that wherever Krishna and Arjuna are found together, there is prosperity, victory, and righteousness — closes the entire text not with abstract philosophy but with a simple, almost proverbial statement about what genuine partnership between the divine and the sincere makes possible.
